Action items assigned for topology diagram, credentials handoff, and a small benchmark plan.\",\n  \"action_items\": [\n    \"Priya Nair: Share VPC peering diagram and AWS account IDs by 2026-04-06\",\n    \"Ethan Cole: Draft pilot benchmark script and sample prompt set by 2026-04-05\",\n    \"Maya Thompson: Send pricing ballpark and pilot contract template by 2026-04-04\",\n    \"Samir Patel: Provide current infra telemetry (p95 latency, token counts) by 2026-04-07\",\n    \"Marta Ivanova: Confirm KMS provider and compliance contacts by 2026-04-09\"\n  ],\n  \"next_steps\": [\n    \"Schedule technical lunch-and-learn for dev team (Ethan + Samir) next week\",\n    \"Redwood to run a 1-hour benchmark in Larkview staging with sample models\",\n    \"Customer to complete security questionnaire and provide network details\"\n  ],\n  \"crm_account_id\": \"CRMA-98421-LARK\",\n  \"transcript\": \"Meeting header:\\nDate: 2026-04-02\\nStart: 16:00 UTC\\nDuration: 1:02\\nAttendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Jordan (CSM), Priya (CTO), Daniel (Head of ML), Samir (DevOps), Olivia (Product), Marta (Security)\\n\\nSummary (auto): Align on onboarding plan, pick deployment mode, list security deliverables.\\n\\n--- Transcript ---\\n[00:00] Maya: Hey everybody, welcome, thanks for making the time. Quick intros, I'll kick it off \\u2014 I'm Maya Thompson, account lead for Larkview.\\n[00:07] Priya: Hi Maya, Priya here. Thanks, excited to finally get this moving.\\n[00:10] Daniel: Daniel Ruiz, head of ML \\u2014 we'll be running the NLU features and some rerankers.\\n[00:14] Samir: Samir, DevOps. I'll own the infra bits.\\n[00:16] Olivia: Olivia, product, hi.\\n[00:18] Marta: Marta, security/compliance.\\n[00:21] Ethan: Ethan Cole, solutions engineer at Redwood. I'll run the benchmarks and the technical runbook.\\n[00:24] Jordan: Jordan Lee, your customer success manager. I'll make sure milestones get tracked.\\n\\n[00:30] Maya: Great. Agenda: 1) run through your priorities and success criteria for the pilot, 2) discuss the deployment options and recommended architecture, 3) security and compliance handoffs, and 4) next steps / timeline. Sound good?\\n[00:41] Priya: Sounds good. High level \\u2014 we want predictable latency for our chat assistant (p95 under 450ms ideally) and we need data residency in us-east-1. Also, we have strict PHI-ish rules, so encryption and audit logs are required.\\n[00:56] Maya: Understood. Redwood has a few ways to do this \\u2014 we can do hosted with strict tenancy, Dedicated pool, or Private VPC/control plane. Ethan, quick summary of tradeoffs?\\n[01:06] Ethan: Yep. Hosted is fastest to stand up but you'll be on shared infra, we do tenant isolation and SOC controls but for PHI we usually recommend Private \\u2014 either VPC-hosted control plane or on-prem depending on your compliance posture. Dedicated gives predictability for throughput but still managed by us. For latency, caching + KV cache (we sometimes see notes where KV got transcribed as K V cash) and batching settings will be key.\\n[01:33] Daniel: If we go private VPC, what's the timeline to get the control plane talking? We're trying to start the pilot in two weeks.\\n[01:39] Ethan: Two weeks is tight but doable for VPC peering if network team is responsive. On-prem would take longer. For the pilot we often start with a hosted sandbox while we parallel the VPC peering setup \\u2014 that gets you an immediate surface for functional tests and then we failover traffic to the private route once peering is live.\\n[02:00] Samir: I want to understand peering vs transit gateway options. We use TGW across accounts. We'll need a diagram of the ports and inbound/outbound paths.\\n[02:08] Maya: We'll share a network topology doc. Priya, can you surface the AWS account IDs and TGW info?\\n[02:13] Priya: Yes, we can. I'll get that to you.\\n[02:16] Marta: On security, we need to verify KMS integration and whether Redwood keys or customer-managed KMS will be used. Also SAML SSO and RBAC for the console access.\\n[02:28] Jordan: We have SSO integrations \\u2014 we support SAML and OIDC, RBAC roles can map to your groups.\\n[02:33] Marta: Also audit logs retention \\u2014 do you retain API-level logs for 13 months?\\n[02:37] Ethan: Default retention is 90 days for the hosted plan; we can offer extended retention as an add-on or through the Private deployment where logs are pushed to your SIEM. We'll capture the compliance package details and send them over.\\n[02:52] Olivia: For the pilot scope, we want 2 use cases: chat assistant for support triage and a reranker for search results. Success = precision lift on reranker + latency under 450ms for chat. Also cost per 1k interactions should be within our projected budget.\\n[03:08] Maya: Good \\u2014 we'll define metrics (latency p50/p95, tokens per session, cost per 1k). Ethan will propose a benchmark script.\\n[03:16] Ethan: I'll create a simple harness that runs your prompt set against two model variants \\u2014 one quantized low-latency, one higher-quality \\u2014 to show tradeoffs. Also will measure cold-start and cache-warm p95.\\n[03:27] Daniel: For reranker, we have a small internal model \\u2014 are you able to host custom models in the pod?\\n[03:31] Ethan: Yes, we can host customer models if they meet size/format requirements. We'll need the model artifact and a brief spec. For the pilot it's easiest to test with our verified catalog models and then swap in your artifact for a second stage.\\n[03:43] Priya: About data flow \\u2014 we want to avoid sending raw PII back to external logs. Is there an option to redact before logs leave the VPC?\\n[03:51] Ethan: On Private, logs can be retained entirely inside your network. For hosted, we offer masking hooks and sampling controls, but full-on redaction is easier to guarantee with VPC/private. We'll put a recommended practice doc together.\\n[04:06] Samir: On ingress, are there any agent dependencies? We run EKS and have a service mesh.\\n[04:11] Ethan: No heavy agents \\u2014 we use standard TLS endpoints. For VPC peering there's a small NAT/proxy configuration for outbound if you want model fetching to go through your proxy. It all goes in the runbook.\\n[04:22] Maya: Ok timeline: We propose start pilot this coming Monday (2026-04-06). Jordan will coordinate. Ethan will run an initial benchmark in staging on Friday and share results. Priya/Samir to share network and account details by Wednesday. Marta to confirm KMS/SOC2 questions by end of next week.\\n[04:40] Priya: Monday is ambitious but we'll aim for it, Samir will prioritize.\\n[04:44] Samir: Ok.\\n[04:46] Olivia: A question on rollouts: if we see quality regressions, do we have an auto rollback?\\n[04:50] Ethan: We support canary rollouts and automatic fallback to a previous model variant. Our console shows per-route metrics and will mark a failed rollout if latency or error rate crosses thresholds.\\n[04:59] Daniel: Great \\u2014 can we capture tokenization parity? We use a custom tokenizer for the reranker.\\n[05:04] Ethan: We'll need a tokenizer spec; tokenization differences can cause token accounting differences which affect cost. We'll add that to the checklist.\\n[05:11] Jordan: Quick note \\u2014 pricing for pilot: we usually provide a short-term credit and then a usage estimate. Maya will send a ballpark and a pilot contract.\\n[05:19] Maya: Yep I'll send that today.\\n[05:22] Priya: Anything else on compliance side? Marta?\\n[05:24] Marta: Please send SOC2, ISO27001, and the pen test summary. Also I'd like the list of sub-processors.\\n[05:31] Maya: We'll attach the compliance pack.\\n[05:33] Ethan: For benchmarks, do you have representative prompt sets?\\n[05:36] Daniel: Yes, I'll share a 200-sample prompt set \\u2014 mixing short chat prompts and long context examples.\\n[05:42] Ethan: Perfect. I'll run them at different concurrency levels to surface p95 at realistic load.\\n[05:48] Samir: On cost optimization, what about quantization and batching tradeoffs?\\n[05:52] Ethan: We'll show configurations. Quantized model + aggressive batching reduces cost but increases latency variance; with prefix caching you can keep p95 low. We'll include a recommended config.\\n[06:04] Olivia: Who will be our day-to-day contacts?\\n[06:07] Maya: Maya for contract/pricing, Jordan for success milestones, Ethan for tech. We'll make an internal contact sheet.\\n[06:12] Priya: Ok sounds good.\\n[06:14] Maya: Quick recap of next steps \\u2014 Priya share network & account IDs by 2026-04-06; Samir provide telemetry; Marta provide KMS and compliance priorities; Ethan draft benchmark and run Friday; Maya send pilot contract and pricing by 2026-04-04; Jordan will schedule the dev lunch-and-learn.\\n[06:34] Daniel: One last thing \\u2014 any special firewall ports?\\n[06:36] Ethan: We'll circulate a small table but typically HTTPS outbound to our endpoint, and if you're doing peering, no public egress is required.\\n[06:44] Priya: Thanks all. Looking forward.\\n[06:46] Maya: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the deck and the action-item list.\\n[06:50] Marta: Thanks.\\n[06:52] Jordan: Bye all.\\n\\nEnd of meeting.\\n\\nReferences shared during call:\\n- \\\"Pilot checklist\\\" doc (link in meeting notes)\\n- Compliance pack (SOC2/ISO) to be attached by Maya\\n- Benchmark harness template (Ethan will provide GitHub gist)\\n\",\n  \"title_field_name\": \"title\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"summary\",\n    \"action_items\",\n    \"next_steps\",\n    \"transcript\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_1ceb67c562a647838ca1b925f4187553\"\n}",

{
  "meeting_id": "m-20260402-larkview-001",
  "recorded_at": "2026-04-02T16:00:00Z",
  "duration_minutes": "62",
  "call_type": "checkin",
  "title": "Larkview HealthTech onboarding & risk handoff",
  "redwood_owner": "Maya Thompson",
  "redwood_attendees": [
    "Maya Thompson (AE)",
    "Ethan Cole (Solutions Engineer)",
    "Jordan Lee (CSM)"
  ],
  "customer_company": "Larkview HealthTech",
  "customer_attendees": [
    "Priya Nair (CTO)",
    "Daniel Ruiz (Head of ML)",
    "Samir Patel (DevOps)",
    "Olivia Grant (Product)",
    "Marta Ivanova (Security)"
  ],
  "transcription_quality": "medium",
  "competitors_mentioned": [
    "AWS Bedrock",
    "Internal infra",
    "Anthropic"
  ],
  "topics": [
    "VPC/private deployment options",
    "SLA and latency targets",
    "Data retention & KMS",
    "Pilot scope & success metrics",
    "Integration checklist"
  ],
  "summary": "Kickoff to align on onboarding timeline, security controls, and pilot success criteria. Redwood AE and SE walked through network architecture options (hosted vs private/VPC vs on-prem container), confirmed security questionnaire next steps, and scoped a two-week pilot focusing on ingest and inference latency targets. Action items assigned for topology diagram, credentials handoff, and a small benchmark plan.",
  "action_items": [
    "Priya Nair: Share VPC peering diagram and AWS account IDs by 2026-04-06",
    "Ethan Cole: Draft pilot benchmark script and sample prompt set by 2026-04-05",
    "Maya Thompson: Send pricing ballpark and pilot contract template by 2026-04-04",
    "Samir Patel: Provide current infra telemetry (p95 latency, token counts) by 2026-04-07",
    "Marta Ivanova: Confirm KMS provider and compliance contacts by 2026-04-09"
  ],
  "next_steps": [
    "Schedule technical lunch-and-learn for dev team (Ethan + Samir) next week",
    "Redwood to run a 1-hour benchmark in Larkview staging with sample models",
    "Customer to complete security questionnaire and provide network details"
  ],
  "crm_account_id": "CRMA-98421-LARK",
  "transcript": "Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-02
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 1:02
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Jordan (CSM), Priya (CTO), Daniel (Head of ML), Samir (DevOps), Olivia (Product), Marta (Security)

Summary (auto): Align on onboarding plan, pick deployment mode, list security deliverables.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Maya: Hey everybody, welcome, thanks for making the time. Quick intros, I'll kick it off — I'm Maya Thompson, account lead for Larkview.
[00:07] Priya: Hi Maya, Priya here. Thanks, excited to finally get this moving.
[00:10] Daniel: Daniel Ruiz, head of ML — we'll be running the NLU features and some rerankers.
[00:14] Samir: Samir, DevOps. I'll own the infra bits.
[00:16] Olivia: Olivia, product, hi.
[00:18] Marta: Marta, security/compliance.
[00:21] Ethan: Ethan Cole, solutions engineer at Redwood. I'll run the benchmarks and the technical runbook.
[00:24] Jordan: Jordan Lee, your customer success manager. I'll make sure milestones get tracked.

[00:30] Maya: Great. Agenda: 1) run through your priorities and success criteria for the pilot, 2) discuss the deployment options and recommended architecture, 3) security and compliance handoffs, and 4) next steps / timeline. Sound good?
[00:41] Priya: Sounds good. High level — we want predictable latency for our chat assistant (p95 under 450ms ideally) and we need data residency in us-east-1. Also, we have strict PHI-ish rules, so encryption and audit logs are required.
[00:56] Maya: Understood. Redwood has a few ways to do this — we can do hosted with strict tenancy, Dedicated pool, or Private VPC/control plane. Ethan, quick summary of tradeoffs?
[01:06] Ethan: Yep. Hosted is fastest to stand up but you'll be on shared infra, we do tenant isolation and SOC controls but for PHI we usually recommend Private — either VPC-hosted control plane or on-prem depending on your compliance posture. Dedicated gives predictability for throughput but still managed by us. For latency, caching + KV cache (we sometimes see notes where KV got transcribed as K V cash) and batching settings will be key.
[01:33] Daniel: If we go private VPC, what's the timeline to get the control plane talking? We're trying to start the pilot in two weeks.
[01:39] Ethan: Two weeks is tight but doable for VPC peering if network team is responsive. On-prem would take longer. For the pilot we often start with a hosted sandbox while we parallel the VPC peering setup — that gets you an immediate surface for functional tests and then we failover traffic to the private route once peering is live.
[02:00] Samir: I want to understand peering vs transit gateway options. We use TGW across accounts. We'll need a diagram of the ports and inbound/outbound paths.
[02:08] Maya: We'll share a network topology doc. Priya, can you surface the AWS account IDs and TGW info?
[02:13] Priya: Yes, we can. I'll get that to you.
[02:16] Marta: On security, we need to verify KMS integration and whether Redwood keys or customer-managed KMS will be used. Also SAML SSO and RBAC for the console access.
[02:28] Jordan: We have SSO integrations — we support SAML and OIDC, RBAC roles can map to your groups.
[02:33] Marta: Also audit logs retention — do you retain API-level logs for 13 months?
[02:37] Ethan: Default retention is 90 days for the hosted plan; we can offer extended retention as an add-on or through the Private deployment where logs are pushed to your SIEM. We'll capture the compliance package details and send them over.
[02:52] Olivia: For the pilot scope, we want 2 use cases: chat assistant for support triage and a reranker for search results. Success = precision lift on reranker + latency under 450ms for chat. Also cost per 1k interactions should be within our projected budget.
[03:08] Maya: Good — we'll define metrics (latency p50/p95, tokens per session, cost per 1k). Ethan will propose a benchmark script.
[03:16] Ethan: I'll create a simple harness that runs your prompt set against two model variants — one quantized low-latency, one higher-quality — to show tradeoffs. Also will measure cold-start and cache-warm p95.
[03:27] Daniel: For reranker, we have a small internal model — are you able to host custom models in the pod?
[03:31] Ethan: Yes, we can host customer models if they meet size/format requirements. We'll need the model artifact and a brief spec. For the pilot it's easiest to test with our verified catalog models and then swap in your artifact for a second stage.
[03:43] Priya: About data flow — we want to avoid sending raw PII back to external logs. Is there an option to redact before logs leave the VPC?
[03:51] Ethan: On Private, logs can be retained entirely inside your network. For hosted, we offer masking hooks and sampling controls, but full-on redaction is easier to guarantee with VPC/private. We'll put a recommended practice doc together.
[04:06] Samir: On ingress, are there any agent dependencies? We run EKS and have a service mesh.
[04:11] Ethan: No heavy agents — we use standard TLS endpoints. For VPC peering there's a small NAT/proxy configuration for outbound if you want model fetching to go through your proxy. It all goes in the runbook.
[04:22] Maya: Ok timeline: We propose start pilot this coming Monday (2026-04-06). Jordan will coordinate. Ethan will run an initial benchmark in staging on Friday and share results. Priya/Samir to share network and account details by Wednesday. Marta to confirm KMS/SOC2 questions by end of next week.
[04:40] Priya: Monday is ambitious but we'll aim for it, Samir will prioritize.
[04:44] Samir: Ok.
[04:46] Olivia: A question on rollouts: if we see quality regressions, do we have an auto rollback?
[04:50] Ethan: We support canary rollouts and automatic fallback to a previous model variant. Our console shows per-route metrics and will mark a failed rollout if latency or error rate crosses thresholds.
[04:59] Daniel: Great — can we capture tokenization parity? We use a custom tokenizer for the reranker.
[05:04] Ethan: We'll need a tokenizer spec; tokenization differences can cause token accounting differences which affect cost. We'll add that to the checklist.
[05:11] Jordan: Quick note — pricing for pilot: we usually provide a short-term credit and then a usage estimate. Maya will send a ballpark and a pilot contract.
[05:19] Maya: Yep I'll send that today.
[05:22] Priya: Anything else on compliance side? Marta?
[05:24] Marta: Please send SOC2, ISO27001, and the pen test summary. Also I'd like the list of sub-processors.
[05:31] Maya: We'll attach the compliance pack.
[05:33] Ethan: For benchmarks, do you have representative prompt sets?
[05:36] Daniel: Yes, I'll share a 200-sample prompt set — mixing short chat prompts and long context examples.
[05:42] Ethan: Perfect. I'll run them at different concurrency levels to surface p95 at realistic load.
[05:48] Samir: On cost optimization, what about quantization and batching tradeoffs?
[05:52] Ethan: We'll show configurations. Quantized model + aggressive batching reduces cost but increases latency variance; with prefix caching you can keep p95 low. We'll include a recommended config.
[06:04] Olivia: Who will be our day-to-day contacts?
[06:07] Maya: Maya for contract/pricing, Jordan for success milestones, Ethan for tech. We'll make an internal contact sheet.
[06:12] Priya: Ok sounds good.
[06:14] Maya: Quick recap of next steps — Priya share network & account IDs by 2026-04-06; Samir provide telemetry; Marta provide KMS and compliance priorities; Ethan draft benchmark and run Friday; Maya send pilot contract and pricing by 2026-04-04; Jordan will schedule the dev lunch-and-learn.
[06:34] Daniel: One last thing — any special firewall ports?
[06:36] Ethan: We'll circulate a small table but typically HTTPS outbound to our endpoint, and if you're doing peering, no public egress is required.
[06:44] Priya: Thanks all. Looking forward.
[06:46] Maya: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the deck and the action-item list.
[06:50] Marta: Thanks.
[06:52] Jordan: Bye all.

Not a final matrix.\\\\n- Focus: areas that tend to be messy for Redwood Private and Dedicated customers (network isolation, key management, customer-managed KMS, and audit logging for private control plane).\\\\n\\\\nNotes to self / immediate asks:\\\\n- Ask SRE: where is the single source for ingress VPC peering docs for Private? I remember two, one in infra space and one in solutions eng. Need canonical link.\\\\n- Ask Platform Eng: can we produce a short statement / diagram that shows control plane separation for Private deployments (control plane in customer VPC vs Redwood-managed control plane)?\\\\n- Verify: Dedicated instances are on reserved GPU pools \\u2014 does that mean we have a documented change management process for capacity changes (approve/notify customers)? Where is evidence of scheduled maintenance notices historically?\\\\n\\\\nHigh-level risks I want captured (raw):\\\\n- Misaligned evidence: security team pulls logs from hosted control plane; customer private deployments use local logging \\u2014 we might not have consolidated retention proof.\\\\n- KMS ambiguity: customers use their own KMS vs Redwood KMS - need to show how keys are handled, rotate, and who has access in emergency.\\\\n- Deployment drift: on-prem packages may be modified by customers; how do we document baseline and patch verification?\\\\n\\\\nControl probe sketches (very rough):\\\\n- C-AUTH-01: SSO/IdP configuration and least-privilege roles\\\\n  - Evidence: SSO policy doc, sample SAML assertion mapping, last 90-day role review log, ticket assigning owner.\\\\n  - Owner: identity team (TBD)\\\\n  - Questions: Do we have automated monthly role recertification or manual? Slack thread about role sweeps?\\\\n\\\\n- C-KMS-02: Key lifecycle for customer-managed KMS & Redwood-managed KMS\\\\n  - Evidence: KMS runbook, rotation schedule, HSM attestation (if used), sample audit log showing key access, KMS IAM policy snapshots.\\\\n  - Owner: infra-crypto (or sec-ops)\\\\n  - Unresolved: for Private deployments where customer brings KMS, what artifacts do we collect to show separation of duties? Customer attestation?\\\\n\\\\n- C-LOG-03: Logging and retention coverage across Hosted / Dedicated / Private\\\\n  - Evidence: index of log sinks (CloudWatch/Stackdriver/ELK), retention config, example log export for a week, retention policy doc, retention expiration alerts.\\\\n  - Owner: observability\\\\n  - Practical: compile 2 weeks of example logs from each product mode, annotate where logs are not central.\\\\n\\\\n- C-CHANGE-04: Change management for runtime or model rollouts that affect inference behavior\\\\n  - Evidence: rollout runbook, canary logs, post-deploy evaluation checklist, rollback ticket template.\\\\n  - Owner: release-engineering\\\\n  - Note: link to rollout automation PRs + console rollout config. Need copy of canary config used in last 3 release cycles.\\\\n\\\\n- C-OPS-05: Incident response and detection coverage for inference runtime (latency/cost/regression incidents)\\\\n  - Evidence: incident report templates, 90/180-day incident list + postmortems, runbook for L7 incidents, contact matrix.\\\\n  - Owner: site-reliability-engineering\\\\n  - Gap: small incidents often handled via Slack threads; need exported timelines for audit.\\\\n\\\\nEvidence naming convention (proposal):\\\\n- Use short structured names to avoid ad-hoc PDFs: e.g. soc2-C-KMS-02-kms-rotation-2025-10-21.log, soc2-C-LOG-03-elk-retention-2026-02-10.json, soc2-C-AUTH-01-role-review-2026-01.csv\\\\n- If we push this naming to owners it will make bulk packaging easier. TODO: ask legal if any artifact should be redacted before sharing with auditors.\\\\n\\\\nQuick mapping for SOC2 criteria (tentative):\\\\n- Security (CC) \\u2014 covers C-AUTH-01, C-KMS-02, C-LOG-03, C-CHANGE-04\\\\n- Availability \\u2014 covers C-OPS-05, C-CHANGE-04\\\\n- Confidentiality \\u2014 covers C-KMS-02, C-LOG-03 (access controls)\\\\n\\\\nQuestions to resolve (prioritize):\\\\n1) Private deployments: do we maintain any remote telemetry by default? If yes, where is the opt-out documented and does that affect evidence collection?\\\\n2) For customer-managed KMS, can customer provide a signed attestation PDF that we can stash in evidence? Is that acceptable to auditors?\\\\n3) Are backups for dedicated clusters encrypted at rest by default? Evidence: backup config snapshot + encryption keys used.\\\\n4) Where are historical maintenance notifications stored for Dedicated (to show communications re: planned downtime)?\\\\n5) For release rollouts that change model weights / quantization, can we produce a small eval script and results bundle that shows pre/post metrics for the change?\\\\n\\\\nQuick TODO list (actionable):\\\\n- [ ] Ping Lena for latest KMS runbook and whether HSM attestation exists (deadline: 2026-03-02)\\\\n- [ ] Export one week of logs from Private demo cluster and annotate missing fields (deadline: 2026-03-07)\\\\n- [ ] Draft naming convention email and circulate to owners (deadline: 2026-03-01)\\\\n- [ ] Collect last three release-engineering canary configs + postmortem (deadline: 2026-03-10)\\\\n- [ ] Ask legal: acceptable customer attestation formats for KMS separation (deadline: 2026-03-04)\\\\n\\\\nRandom brainstorm (raw):\\\\n- Could we create a \\u2018SOC2-light snapshot\\u2019 tool that collects a predefined evidence bundle from a customer-controlled Private deployment (with their consent) and outputs a zip of named artifacts? This would accelerate evidence pulls for renewals.\\\\n- Consider small agent that runs on Private installs to verify baseline binaries/hashes and returns signed attestations to Redwood (opt-in only).\\\\n\\\\nNotes-to-self (formatting + handoff):\\\\n- When packaging artifacts for auditors, include a 1-pager per control that lists: objective, tested evidence names (with timestamps), owner, and any compensating controls. Keep it short.\\\\n- Avoid sending raw Slack exports unless cleaned and annotated. Summarize threads with links to ticket IDs.\\\\n\\\\nEnd \\u2014 capture followups here so I can transfer to a formal Confluence control page after I have the first round of artifacts.\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n\",\n  \"title_field_name\": \"title\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"content\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_c0a03597cb93476b9904666e1aedd6e0\"\n}",

  "content": "Purpose / quick context:\\n- Short, informal scratch to capture immediate questions and simple mappings to speed up an evidence collection spike for SOC2 scoping. Not a final matrix.\\n- Focus: areas that tend to be messy for Redwood Private and Dedicated customers (network isolation, key management, customer-managed KMS, and audit logging for private control plane).\\n\\nNotes to self / immediate asks:\\n- Ask SRE: where is the single source for ingress VPC peering docs for Private? I remember two, one in infra space and one in solutions eng. Need canonical link.\\n- Ask Platform Eng: can we produce a short statement / diagram that shows control plane separation for Private deployments (control plane in customer VPC vs Redwood-managed control plane)?\\n- Verify: Dedicated instances are on reserved GPU pools \u2014 does that mean we have a documented change management process for capacity changes (approve/notify customers)? Where is evidence of scheduled maintenance notices historically?\\n\\nHigh-level risks I want captured (raw):\\n- Misaligned evidence: security team pulls logs from hosted control plane; customer private deployments use local logging \u2014 we might not have consolidated retention proof.\\n- KMS ambiguity: customers use their own KMS vs Redwood KMS - need to show how keys are handled, rotate, and who has access in emergency.\\n- Deployment drift: on-prem packages may be modified by customers; how do we document baseline and patch verification?\\n\\nControl probe sketches (very rough):\\n- C-AUTH-01: SSO/IdP configuration and least-privilege roles\\n  - Evidence: SSO policy doc, sample SAML assertion mapping, last 90-day role review log, ticket assigning owner.\\n  - Owner: identity team (TBD)\\n  - Questions: Do we have automated monthly role recertification or manual? Slack thread about role sweeps?\\n\\n- C-KMS-02: Key lifecycle for customer-managed KMS & Redwood-managed KMS\\n  - Evidence: KMS runbook, rotation schedule, HSM attestation (if used), sample audit log showing key access, KMS IAM policy snapshots.\\n  - Owner: infra-crypto (or sec-ops)\\n  - Unresolved: for Private deployments where customer brings KMS, what artifacts do we collect to show separation of duties? Customer attestation?\\n\\n- C-LOG-03: Logging and retention coverage across Hosted / Dedicated / Private\\n  - Evidence: index of log sinks (CloudWatch/Stackdriver/ELK), retention config, example log export for a week, retention policy doc, retention expiration alerts.\\n  - Owner: observability\\n  - Practical: compile 2 weeks of example logs from each product mode, annotate where logs are not central.\\n\\n- C-CHANGE-04: Change management for runtime or model rollouts that affect inference behavior\\n  - Evidence: rollout runbook, canary logs, post-deploy evaluation checklist, rollback ticket template.\\n  - Owner: release-engineering\\n  - Note: link to rollout automation PRs + console rollout config. Need copy of canary config used in last 3 release cycles.\\n\\n- C-OPS-05: Incident response and detection coverage for inference runtime (latency/cost/regression incidents)\\n  - Evidence: incident report templates, 90/180-day incident list + postmortems, runbook for L7 incidents, contact matrix.\\n  - Owner: site-reliability-engineering\\n  - Gap: small incidents often handled via Slack threads; need exported timelines for audit.\\n\\nEvidence naming convention (proposal):\\n- Use short structured names to avoid ad-hoc PDFs: e.g. soc2-C-KMS-02-kms-rotation-2025-10-21.log, soc2-C-LOG-03-elk-retention-2026-02-10.json, soc2-C-AUTH-01-role-review-2026-01.csv\\n- If we push this naming to owners it will make bulk packaging easier. TODO: ask legal if any artifact should be redacted before sharing with auditors.\\n\\nQuick mapping for SOC2 criteria (tentative):\\n- Security (CC) \u2014 covers C-AUTH-01, C-KMS-02, C-LOG-03, C-CHANGE-04\\n- Availability \u2014 covers C-OPS-05, C-CHANGE-04\\n- Confidentiality \u2014 covers C-KMS-02, C-LOG-03 (access controls)\\n\\nQuestions to resolve (prioritize):\\n1) Private deployments: do we maintain any remote telemetry by default? If yes, where is the opt-out documented and does that affect evidence collection?\\n2) For customer-managed KMS, can customer provide a signed attestation PDF that we can stash in evidence? Is that acceptable to auditors?\\n3) Are backups for dedicated clusters encrypted at rest by default? Evidence: backup config snapshot + encryption keys used.\\n4) Where are historical maintenance notifications stored for Dedicated (to show communications re: planned downtime)?\\n5) For release rollouts that change model weights / quantization, can we produce a small eval script and results bundle that shows pre/post metrics for the change?\\n\\nQuick TODO list (actionable):\\n- [ ] Ping Lena for latest KMS runbook and whether HSM attestation exists (deadline: 2026-03-02)\\n- [ ] Export one week of logs from Private demo cluster and annotate missing fields (deadline: 2026-03-07)\\n- [ ] Draft naming convention email and circulate to owners (deadline: 2026-03-01)\\n- [ ] Collect last three release-engineering canary configs + postmortem (deadline: 2026-03-10)\\n- [ ] Ask legal: acceptable customer attestation formats for KMS separation (deadline: 2026-03-04)\\n\\nRandom brainstorm (raw):\\n- Could we create a \u2018SOC2-light snapshot\u2019 tool that collects a predefined evidence bundle from a customer-controlled Private deployment (with their consent) and outputs a zip of named artifacts? This would accelerate evidence pulls for renewals.\\n- Consider small agent that runs on Private installs to verify baseline binaries/hashes and returns signed attestations to Redwood (opt-in only).\\n\\nNotes-to-self (formatting + handoff):\\n- When packaging artifacts for auditors, include a 1-pager per control that lists: objective, tested evidence names (with timestamps), owner, and any compensating controls. Keep it short.\\n- Avoid sending raw Slack exports unless cleaned and annotated. Summarize threads with links to ticket IDs.\\n\\nEnd \u2014 capture followups here so I can transfer to a formal Confluence control page after I have the first round of artifacts.\\n\\n\\n",

    "content": "{\n  \"channel\": \"product\",\n  \"thread_ts\": \"1767123456\",\n  \"first_message_ts\": \"1767123456\",\n  \"last_message_ts\": \"1767123580\",\n  \"participants\": [\n    \"elaine - PM\",\n    \"armando - Eng\",\n    \"priya - Arch\",\n    \"matt - SRE\",\n    \"ops-bot\"\n  ],\n  \"messages\": \"elaine - PM: Quick sync \\u2014 CS escalated: a large customer needs strict per-region data residency plus a tenant-level SLA. They want a proposal with scope, launch criteria, and cost implications by EOW. @armando @priya can you sketch feasibility?\\n\\narmando - Eng: We can support per-region residency, but it requires routing templates + tenant slices. Rough ballpark: 3 sprints for a pilot path (routing + metadata plumbing) + 1 sprint for canary/telemetry. Main dev work: routing policy DSL, tenant affinity, and a fallback lane.\\n\\npriya - Arch: Agree. Key architecture notes:\\n- We need a routing decision layer that can do region pins, plus affinity windows for sticky KV caches.\\n- Cross-region KV cache invalidation is the trickiest risk for correctness and cost.\\n- Also consider quota/ejection policy when capacity is constrained (evict to fallback model or region).\\n\\nmatt - SRE: Operational constraints: \\n- SLAs require reserved capacity or Dedicated pools; hosted without commitments can\\u2019t guarantee >99.9.\\n- We need an evacuation playbook if a region loses capacity (auto-fail to fallback lane).\\n- Observability: token-level metering by tenant+region.\\n\\nelaine - PM: Customer says they'd pay for Dedicated but wants an initial hosted pilot to feel it out. Proposal: pilot using a small Dedicated slice + hosted fallback. If pilot passes, scale to Dedicated commit. We need acceptance criteria.\\n\\narmando - Eng: Draft acceptance criteria snippet:```\\nAC-1: Requests with region pinning are routed to the pinned region >99% of the time.\\nAC-2: When pinned region is healthy, within-region p95 latency <= 150ms (text gen baseline).\\nAC-3: Fallback behavior tested: on region drain, requests route to fallback with explicit audit log and no unhandled errors.\\nAC-4: Billing for residency (per-region surcharge + reserved capacity metering) is validated end-to-end.\\nAC-5: Canary: 5% traffic for 2 days with telemetry checks (error rate, latency, cost delta).\\n```\\n\\npriya - Arch: Add gating for correctness: unit tests + integration scenarios for KV cache consistency across slices. Also require a migration plan for customers who later change pinned region (data residency window).\\n\\nmatt - SRE: Runbook items to add: evacuation checklist, step to toggle fallback lane, metrics dashboards + alerts (p95, 5xx, queue depth by tenant/region). Ops automation for capacity bump must be exercised in pilot.\\n\\nops-bot: note: billing team notified \\u2014 invoice schema will need region labels and reserved capacity line items.\\n\\nelaine - PM: Decision draft: pilot Q3 (target kickoff in 3 weeks). Owners: Armando (engineering lead), Priya (architecture + gating), Matt (SRE/runbooks), Elaine (product & customer liaison). Deliverables by end of pilot: spec, canary runbook, telemetry dashboard, billing mapping, and customer-facing runbook.\\n\\narmando - Eng: +1 on timeline. Need a small infra spike to validate routing DSL changes; will schedule this week.\\n\\npriya - Arch: I'll write the migration/misalignment doc and a compatibility matrix for fallback models.\\n\\nmatt - SRE: I'll prepare the canary dashboard and a synthetic traffic harness for the 5% test.\\n\\nelaine - PM: I'll draft the spec doc and send to the customer for alignment. Action items and owners in a Google doc \\u2014 I'll share link later. :thumbsup:\\n\\narmando - Eng: one open question \\u2014 pricing model for residency surcharge: fixed per-region reserve vs usage-based delta. We should present both.\\n\\nelaine - PM: Good point. Priya/matt, include cost sensitivity tests in the canary so CS has data to pick model.\\n\\npriya - Arch: noted. Also adding a low-cost degraded mode: if dedicated capacity exhausted, degrade to a quantized model variant to preserve availability, and surface quality metrics.\\n\\nmatt - SRE: ack. That gives us three fallback tiers: same-region Dedicated, cross-region fallback, and degraded-model fallback. We'll test all three in canary.\\n\\nelaine - PM: Thanks team. I'll compile these notes into the spec and post the doc by EOD. If anyone needs to change scope, flag here before I share with CS. :spiral_calendar:\\n\\narmando - Eng: sounds good.\\n\\npriya - Arch: lgtm.\\n\\nmatt - SRE: lgtm.\",\n  \"title_field_name\": \"channel\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"messages\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_d9a15ab8f79c4c7e938f90cf3586da13\"\n}",

{
  "channel": "product",
  "thread_ts": "1767123456",
  "first_message_ts": "1767123456",
  "last_message_ts": "1767123580",
  "participants": [
    "elaine - PM",
    "armando - Eng",
    "priya - Arch",
    "matt - SRE",
    "ops-bot"
  ],
  "messages": "elaine - PM: Quick sync — CS escalated: a large customer needs strict per-region data residency plus a tenant-level SLA. They want a proposal with scope, launch criteria, and cost implications by EOW. @armando @priya can you sketch feasibility?

armando - Eng: We can support per-region residency, but it requires routing templates + tenant slices. Rough ballpark: 3 sprints for a pilot path (routing + metadata plumbing) + 1 sprint for canary/telemetry. Main dev work: routing policy DSL, tenant affinity, and a fallback lane.

priya - Arch: Agree. Key architecture notes:
- We need a routing decision layer that can do region pins, plus affinity windows for sticky KV caches.
- Cross-region KV cache invalidation is the trickiest risk for correctness and cost.
- Also consider quota/ejection policy when capacity is constrained (evict to fallback model or region).

matt - SRE: Operational constraints: 
- SLAs require reserved capacity or Dedicated pools; hosted without commitments can’t guarantee >99.9.
- We need an evacuation playbook if a region loses capacity (auto-fail to fallback lane).
- Observability: token-level metering by tenant+region.

elaine - PM: Customer says they'd pay for Dedicated but wants an initial hosted pilot to feel it out. Proposal: pilot using a small Dedicated slice + hosted fallback. If pilot passes, scale to Dedicated commit. We need acceptance criteria.

armando - Eng: Draft acceptance criteria snippet:```
AC-1: Requests with region pinning are routed to the pinned region >99% of the time.
AC-2: When pinned region is healthy, within-region p95 latency <= 150ms (text gen baseline).
AC-3: Fallback behavior tested: on region drain, requests route to fallback with explicit audit log and no unhandled errors.
AC-4: Billing for residency (per-region surcharge + reserved capacity metering) is validated end-to-end.
AC-5: Canary: 5% traffic for 2 days with telemetry checks (error rate, latency, cost delta).
```

priya - Arch: Add gating for correctness: unit tests + integration scenarios for KV cache consistency across slices. Also require a migration plan for customers who later change pinned region (data residency window).

matt - SRE: Runbook items to add: evacuation checklist, step to toggle fallback lane, metrics dashboards + alerts (p95, 5xx, queue depth by tenant/region). Ops automation for capacity bump must be exercised in pilot.

ops-bot: note: billing team notified — invoice schema will need region labels and reserved capacity line items.

elaine - PM: Decision draft: pilot Q3 (target kickoff in 3 weeks). Owners: Armando (engineering lead), Priya (architecture + gating), Matt (SRE/runbooks), Elaine (product & customer liaison). Deliverables by end of pilot: spec, canary runbook, telemetry dashboard, billing mapping, and customer-facing runbook.

armando - Eng: +1 on timeline. Need a small infra spike to validate routing DSL changes; will schedule this week.

priya - Arch: I'll write the migration/misalignment doc and a compatibility matrix for fallback models.

matt - SRE: I'll prepare the canary dashboard and a synthetic traffic harness for the 5% test.

elaine - PM: I'll draft the spec doc and send to the customer for alignment. Action items and owners in a Google doc — I'll share link later. :thumbsup:

armando - Eng: one open question — pricing model for residency surcharge: fixed per-region reserve vs usage-based delta. We should present both.

elaine - PM: Good point. Priya/matt, include cost sensitivity tests in the canary so CS has data to pick model.

priya - Arch: noted. Also adding a low-cost degraded mode: if dedicated capacity exhausted, degrade to a quantized model variant to preserve availability, and surface quality metrics.

matt - SRE: ack. That gives us three fallback tiers: same-region Dedicated, cross-region fallback, and degraded-model fallback. We'll test all three in canary.

elaine - PM: Thanks team. I'll compile these notes into the spec and post the doc by EOD. If anyone needs to change scope, flag here before I share with CS. :spiral_calendar:

armando - Eng: sounds good.

priya - Arch: lgtm.

matt - SRE: lgtm.",

  "content_field_names": [
    "messages"
  ],
  "dataset_doc_uuid": "dsid_d9a15ab8f79c4c7e938f90cf3586da13"
}

# Hosted API retention rule

Status: Support-facing interim rule (v1)  
Owner: Platform & Console — Ethan Park  
Last validated: 2026-08-01

## Supported guidance

- Hosted API-level logs are retained for 90 days by default.
- Longer log retention may be available as an add-on. Private deployments can instead forward logs to a customer SIEM; support must confirm the applicable order form and deployment configuration before promising either option.
- Treat configured region and runtime fallback as separate controls. Product acceptance criteria require fallback routing to produce an explicit audit event. This evidence does **not** establish that standard Hosted API data is region-locked or that fallback never crosses regions.
- For audit validation, collect the retention configuration, a representative log export, the retention-policy document, and retention-expiration alerts. The assurance memo is a draft evidence checklist, not a customer commitment.

## Unknowns — do not promise

Current evidence does not establish:

- retention periods for request or response payloads, embeddings, model artifacts, or aggregated metrics;
- deletion timing for active indexes, primary stores, caches, analytics copies, snapshots, or backups;
- timing after tenant termination or an erasure request;
- whether backups replicate across regions, their maximum retention, or whether an EU-only/US-only custody option covers backups;
- availability, format, or retention of deletion receipts, certificates, or customer-visible audit events;
- a default Hosted API storage country or a contractual residency guarantee.

Support must not translate the 90-day API-log statement into a purge SLA or a payload-retention promise.

## Validation before answering a questionnaire

1. Identify Hosted, Dedicated, or Private deployment and obtain the executed order form/DPA and any residency amendment.
2. Confirm the exact data class: API metadata, prompt/response payload, embedding, artifact, audit event, cache, analytic copy, or backup.
3. Ask Platform/SRE for the deployed retention configuration and expiration-job evidence.
4. Ask Security/Privacy for approved deletion, backup, residency, and attestation language.
5. For residency, verify both the primary region and every fallback/DR and backup path.
6. Escalate any requested deletion or residency SLA until a controlling policy or contract is cited.

## Evidence

- [Larkview HealthTech onboarding & risk handoff](/knowledge/company/sources/fireflies/customer-success/2026-04-02-larkview-healthtech-onboarding-risk-handoff.json) (`dsid_1ceb67c562a647838ca1b925f4187553`): Redwood states a 90-day default for hosted API-level logs; extended retention is an add-on, and Private can push logs to the customer SIEM. Transcript quality is marked medium.

- [Assurance micro memo: quick SOC 2 control probes](/knowledge/company/sources/google_drive/users/assurance-micro-memo-haruki-2026.json) (`dsid_c0a03597cb93476b9904666e1aedd6e0`): draft checklist for retention-control evidence and unresolved assurance questions.

# Hosted API retention rule

Status: Support-facing interim rule (v1)  
Owner: Platform & Console — Ethan Park  
Last validated: 2026-08-01

## Supported guidance

- Hosted API-level logs are retained for 90 days by default.
- Longer log retention may be available as an add-on. Private deployments can instead forward logs to a customer SIEM; support must confirm the applicable order form and deployment configuration before promising either option.
- Treat configured region and runtime fallback as separate controls. Product acceptance criteria require fallback routing to produce an explicit audit event. This evidence does **not** establish that standard Hosted API data is region-locked or that fallback never crosses regions.
- For audit validation, collect the retention configuration, a representative log export, the retention-policy document, and retention-expiration alerts. The assurance memo is a draft evidence checklist, not a customer commitment.

## Unknowns — do not promise

Current evidence does not establish:

- retention periods for request or response payloads, embeddings, model artifacts, or aggregated metrics;
- deletion timing for active indexes, primary stores, caches, analytics copies, snapshots, or backups;
- timing after tenant termination or an erasure request;
- whether backups replicate across regions, their maximum retention, or whether an EU-only/US-only custody option covers backups;
- availability, format, or retention of deletion receipts, certificates, or customer-visible audit events;
- a default Hosted API storage country or a contractual residency guarantee.

Support must not translate the 90-day API-log statement into a purge SLA or a payload-retention promise.

## Validation before answering a questionnaire

- availability, format, or retention of deletion receipts, certificates, or customer-visible audit events;
- a default Hosted API storage country or a contractual residency guarantee.

Support must not translate the 90-day API-log statement into a purge SLA or a payload-retention promise.

## Validation before answering a questionnaire

1. Identify Hosted, Dedicated, or Private deployment and obtain the executed order form/DPA and any residency amendment.
2. Confirm the exact data class: API metadata, prompt/response payload, embedding, artifact, audit event, cache, analytic copy, or backup.
3. Ask Platform/SRE for the deployed retention configuration and expiration-job evidence.
4. Ask Security/Privacy for approved deletion, backup, residency, and attestation language.
5. For residency, verify both the primary region and every fallback/DR and backup path.
6. Escalate any requested deletion or residency SLA until a controlling policy or contract is cited.

Transcript quality is marked medium.
- [Residency fallback pricing and launch acceptance criteria](/knowledge/company/sources/slack/product/1767123456-residency-fallback-pricing-and-launch-ask-negotiation.json) (`dsid_d9a15ab8f79c4c7e938f90cf3586da13`): fallback must be tested and explicitly audit-logged; it does not itself establish a residency promise.

# Hosted API retention rule

Status: Support-facing interim rule (v1)  
Owner: Platform & Console — Ethan Park  
Last validated: 2026-08-01

## Supported guidance

- Hosted API-level logs are retained for 90 days by default.
- Longer log retention may be available as an add-on. Private deployments can instead forward logs to a customer SIEM; support must confirm the applicable order form and deployment configuration before promising either option.
- Treat configured region and runtime fallback as separate controls. Product acceptance criteria require fallback routing to produce an explicit audit event. This evidence does **not** establish that standard Hosted API data is region-locked or that fallback never crosses regions.
- For audit validation, collect the retention configuration, a representative log export, the retention-policy document, and retention-expiration alerts. The assurance memo is a draft evidence checklist, not a customer commitment.

## Unknowns — do not promise

Current evidence does not establish:

- retention periods for request or response payloads, embeddings, model artifacts, or aggregated metrics;
- deletion timing for active indexes, primary stores, caches, analytics copies, snapshots, or backups;
- timing after tenant termination or an erasure request;
- whether backups replicate across regions, their maximum retention, or whether an EU-only/US-only custody option covers backups;
- availability, format, or retention of deletion receipts, certificates, or customer-visible audit events;
- a default Hosted API storage country or a contractual residency guarantee.

Support must not translate the 90-day API-log statement into a purge SLA or a payload-retention promise.

## Validation before answering a questionnaire

result.title: Hosted API retention rule
result.text:
[Document context]
Title: Hosted API retention rule
Source: Redwood Platform & Console
Path: /knowledge/policies/hosted-api-retention.md
Workspace: task/ethan-park/retention-rule-v1-v3

# Hosted API retention rule

Status: Support-facing interim rule (v1)  
Owner: Platform & Console — Ethan Park  
Last validated: 2026-08-01

## Supported guidance

- Hosted API-level logs are retained for 90 days by default.
- Longer log retention may be available as an add-on. Private deployments can instead forward logs to a customer SIEM; support must confirm the applicable order form and deployment configuration before promising either option.
- Treat configured region and runtime fallback as separate controls. Product acceptance criteria require fallback routing to produce an explicit audit event. This evidence does **not** establish that standard Hosted API data is region-locked or that fallback never crosses regions.
- For audit validation, collect the retention configuration, a representative log export, the retention-policy document, and retention-expiration alerts. The assurance memo is a draft evidence checklist, not a customer commitment.

## Unknowns — do not promise

Current evidence does not establish:

- retention periods for request or response payloads, embeddings, model artifacts, or aggregated metrics;
- deletion timing for active indexes, primary stores, caches, analytics copies, snapshots, or backups;
- timing after tenant termination or an erasure request;
- whether backups replicate across regions, their maximum retention, or whether an EU-only/US-only custody option covers backups;
- availability, format, or retention of deletion receipts, certificates, or customer-visible audit events;
- a default Hosted API storage country or a contractual residency guarantee.

Support must not translate the 90-day API-log statement into a purge SLA or a payload-retention promise.

## Validation before answering a questionnaire

# Hosted API retention rule

Status: Support-facing interim rule (v1)  
Owner: Platform & Console — Ethan Park  
Last validated: 2026-08-01

## Supported guidance

- Hosted API-level logs are retained for 90 days by default.
- Longer log retention may be available as an add-on. Private deployments can instead forward logs to a customer SIEM; support must confirm the applicable order form and deployment configuration before promising either option.
- Treat configured region and runtime fallback as separate controls. Product acceptance criteria require fallback routing to produce an explicit audit event. This evidence does **not** establish that standard Hosted API data is region-locked or that fallback never crosses regions.
- For audit validation, collect the retention configuration, a representative log export, the retention-policy document, and retention-expiration alerts. The assurance memo is a draft evidence checklist, not a customer commitment.

## Unknowns — do not promise

Current evidence does not establish:

- retention periods for request or response payloads, embeddings, model artifacts, or aggregated metrics;
- deletion timing for active indexes, primary stores, caches, analytics copies, snapshots, or backups;
- timing after tenant termination or an erasure request;
- whether backups replicate across regions, their maximum retention, or whether an EU-only/US-only custody option covers backups;
- availability, format, or retention of deletion receipts, certificates, or customer-visible audit events;
- a default Hosted API storage country or a contractual residency guarantee.

Support must not translate the 90-day API-log statement into a purge SLA or a payload-retention promise.

## Validation before answering a questionnaire",

# Hosted API retention rule

Status: Support-facing interim rule (v1)  
Owner: Platform & Console — Ethan Park  
Last validated: 2026-08-01

## Supported guidance

- Hosted API-level logs are retained for 90 days by default.
- Longer log retention may be available as an add-on. Private deployments can instead forward logs to a customer SIEM; support must confirm the applicable order form and deployment configuration before promising either option.
- Treat configured region and runtime fallback as separate controls. Product acceptance criteria require fallback routing to produce an explicit audit event. This evidence does **not** establish that standard Hosted API data is region-locked or that fallback never crosses regions.
- For audit validation, collect the retention configuration, a representative log export, the retention-policy document, and retention-expiration alerts. The assurance memo is a draft evidence checklist, not a customer commitment.

## Unknowns — do not promise

Current evidence does not establish:

- retention periods for request or response payloads, embeddings, model artifacts, or aggregated metrics;
- deletion timing for active indexes, primary stores, caches, analytics copies, snapshots, or backups;
- timing after tenant termination or an erasure request;
- whether backups replicate across regions, their maximum retention, or whether an EU-only/US-only custody option covers backups;
- availability, format, or retention of deletion receipts, certificates, or customer-visible audit events;
- a default Hosted API storage country or a contractual residency guarantee.

Support must not translate the 90-day API-log statement into a purge SLA or a payload-retention promise.

## Validation before answering a questionnaire

## Validation before answering a questionnaire

4. Ask Security/Privacy for approved deletion, backup, residency, and attestation language.
5. For residency, verify both the primary region and every fallback/DR and backup path.
6. Escalate any requested deletion or residency SLA until a controlling policy or contract is cited.

    "From: Emma Lopez <emma.lopez@crestline.health>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 30 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API - quick Q on data geography & TTL for security questionnaire

Hi Olga,

We're finalizing our vendor security questionnaire for the Crestline June board packet and have a handful of specific items on data geography, default retention, and deletion timelines for hosted APIs. Can you confirm the following for Redwood's hosted offering?

1) Are customer request/response payloads stored at rest? If so, where (region/country) by default and can we request EU-only storage?
2) What are your default retention windows for request logs, embeddings, and model artifacts?
3) After we terminate a tenant or request erasure, what is the timeline for purging primary stores and backups?
4) Do backups/snapshots replicate cross-region? If so, what is the maximum retention on backups?
5) What controls exist for key management (KMS/HSM) and audit logs for deletion events?

I attached our short questionnaire (crestline-sq.pdf) with the same fields. We need a short written response to include in the packet by COB Tuesday.

Thanks,

Olga — draft answers and rationale below. I kept the language concise for inclusion in their packet; we can expand in the appendix if they want implementation details.

1) Storage location by default- Hosted API request/response payloads and generated artifacts are persisted in the tenancy's primary region. For self‑serve accounts we default to the region closest to the sign‑up location (US-west for NA customers). For customers requiring EU-only storage we offer EU tenancy pinning as part of the hosted-enterprise contract (data residency addendum).

2) Default retention windows (hosted API)
- Request/response logs (application payloads): default 30 days; configurable to 90/365 via contract for enterprise plans.
- Streaming/KV caches: ephemeral, retained only in memory and short local caches (<1 hour) unless explicitly persisted by customer choice.
- Embeddings & derived vectors: default 14 days; can be configured to 7 days (strict ephemeral) or retained longer if customer elects persistent vector storage under SLA.
- Model artifacts (snapshots, fine‑tuned artifacts): retained until explicitly deleted; default snapshot retention 30 days for rolling backups.

3) Erasure / tenant termination timelines
- On an account termination/erasure request we stop serving traffic immediately and mark tenant datasets for purge. Primary store purge: typical completion within 30 days.
- Backups / long‑term snapshots: fully scrubbed within 90 days (this accounts for cross‑region replication and backup windows). We provide a certificate of deletion on request after completion.

4) Backups & cross‑region replication
- Backups are scheduled per tenancy and may replicate to a secondary region for disaster recovery depending on the customer's SLA. For customers who require EU‑only custody we ensure backups remain in‑region; cross‑region replication is disabled unless explicitly contracted.
- Maximum backup retention default is 90 days; longer retention available under contract.

5) Key management & auditability
- KMS: Redwood uses cloud KMS by default for encryption at rest; enterprise customers can provide customer‑managed keys (CMKs) or integrate with HSMs in private deployments.
- Audit logs: deletion and erasure events are logged and retained for 365 days by default in our audit trail (accessible to customers via the console for enterprise accounts). Logs include the user, timestamp, object id, and operation status.

Notes on evidence: I attached the small residency matrix and architecture diagram if they want an appendix entry. Suggest we offer Crestline the EU tenancy addendum and a 30‑day primary purge / 90‑day backup scrub cadence in writing; that should be acceptable for their board.

Below is a pragmatic breakdown you can share with legal/compliance. I kept it concise and highlighted tradeoffs. Attaching a short playbook (redwood-sanitization-options-v1.pdf) and an example audit export.\\n\\nRetention (recommended default tiers)\\n- 30 days: lowest cost + simplest (good for ephemeral chat/triage). Minimal log retention, fast KV-cache eviction.\\n- 90 days: common compromise for non-longitudinal PHI artifacts (summaries, annotations). Allows short-term troubleshooting and A/B quality checks.\\n- 365 days: used when business/legal requires year-long traces (billing disputes, clinical continuity). Higher storage and audit complexity.\\nTradeoffs: shorter windows reduce storage and retention of cached embeddings; longer windows increase cost and require stronger key management and rotation policies.\\n\\nSanitization / Redaction options we support\\n1) Pre-ingest field-level redaction: non-reversible removal of named fields before any tokenization or embedding. Strongest guarantee if done client-side or at gateway.\\n2) Server-side deterministic pseudonymization: replace identifiers with consistent pseudonyms (useful when you need linkage but not original value). Reversibility depends on where the mapping store lives \\u2014 we recommend customer-managed KMS + mapping store for reversible mapping.\\n3) Tokenization (reversible): we can integrate with customer token vaults (customer-managed) for reversible tokens; requires contractual controls if reversible.\\n4) Post-ingest scrub + reingest: we support a scrub pipeline that can retroactively remove fields and then re-ingest sanitized artifacts \\u2014 works for stored artifacts but not for in-memory KV cache unless cache flush is triggered (see below).\\n\\nCache/Runtime considerations\\n- KV cache: we provide an API to invalidate/flush per-tenant caches. Flushing is immediate for active processes but you should plan a short rollback window if you rely on prefix caching for latency.\\n- Embeddings and derived artifacts: if embeddings were persisted externally (DB or vector store) we provide scripts and tooling to locate and remove vectors by metadata tag. Note that embeddings derived from sensitive text are irreversible; redaction removes the original text but cannot 'ungenerate' vectors already used by downstream stores without explicit deletion.\\n\\nAuditability / Evidence for audits\\n- Exportable audit logs: timestamped events (object created, deleted, redaction applied, cache flush) with request IDs. Provided as CSV/JSON exports.\\n- Deletion proof: we can provide signed deletion events (hash+timestamp) for storage objects.\\n- Access logs: token-level access trails available via Console with retention window matching your plan.\\n\\nNext steps: I copied Marissa to coordinate Contract/SOW needs and Rishi (our security lead) to chime in on the KMS/mapping specifics. Would you like 30 minutes tomorrow or Friday for a quick walkthrough?\\n\\nRegards,\\nBen Carter\\nAccount Executive, Redwood Inference\\nben_carter@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0189\\n\\nAttachments: redwood-sanitization-options-v1.pdf (PDF), example-audit-log-export.csv (CSV)\\n\",\n    \"From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>\\nTo: Sarah Mills <sarah.mills@harborhealthcare.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>\\nDate: Tue, 08 Jul 2025 11:02:00 -07:00\\nSubject: Re: Data residency/retention and redaction options for PHI - quick questions\\n\\nThanks for the context, Sarah. From a commercial perspective: if Harbor wants a 365-day retention with customer-managed KMS and audit retention for 3 years, we can scope that as a Dedicated + Private-control-plane deployment in the SOW (we'll include a compliance addendum). We often propose a two-stage pricing: base platform + add-on for extended audit exports.\\n\\nIf you confirm the preferred retention tier, I'll draft a one-page SOW and loop legal.\\n\\n\\u2014Marissa\\nMarissa Cole, Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference\\nmarissa_cole@redwood.ai\\n\",\n    \"From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>\\nTo: Sarah Mills <sarah.mills@harborhealthcare.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>\\nDate: Wed, 09 Jul 2025 08:41:00 -07:00\\nSubject: Re: Data residency/retention and redaction options for PHI - quick questions\\n\\nHi Sarah \\u2014 Rishi from Security. A few technical clarifications to help your controls team evaluate risk: \\n\\n1) Strongest guarantees: pre-ingest client-side redaction or gateway-level transformation (never leave original data on disk) is the most robust for regulated PHI. If you must preserve originals, keep mapping tokens in customer-owned stores (VPC-hosted DB) with strict KMS access.\\n\\n2) Retroactive removal: we can delete objects and issue signed deletion receipts. For runtime artifacts:\\n   - KV cache: we support tenant-scoped eviction calls (immediate). We persist cache-invalidation events to audit logs.\\n   - Worker / GPU memory: clearing memory is immediate but cannot be retroactively validated after process termination; rely on deletion receipts for persisted artifacts.\\n\\n3) Embeddings: treat them as primary artifacts \\u2014 if you need them removed, we will run metadata-tag based deletion across vector stores and provide a deletion report. Note: if third-party vector stores exist outside the Redwood environment, deletion will require coordination.\\n\\n4) Proof for auditors: we provide\\n   - Signed deletion receipts (SHA256 digest + timestamp + signer id)\\n   - Exportable audit logs with event types and correlation IDs\\n   - Evidence of KMS rotations and CMK metadata (when customer-managed KMS is used)\\n\\n5) Operational playbook we recommend for regulated workflows:\\n   - Define retention tier per artifact class (raw transcript, summary, annotations, embeddings)\\n   - Enforce client-side redaction for raw identifiers where possible\\n   - Use pseudonymization for analytics cohorts where linkage is needed\\n   - Schedule regular deletion jobs and capture signed receipts\\n   - Monitor cache eviction and record events in the audit stream\\n\\nI can walk your engineers through the KMS integration and the deletion API. If Harbor needs us to run a one-off scrub to bring an existing dataset into compliance, we will propose a timeboxed engagement with a deletion report.\\n\\n\\u2014Rishi Malhotra\\nHead of Security, Redwood Inference\\nrishi_malhotra@redwood.ai\\n\",\n    \"From: Sarah Mills <sarah.mills@harborhealthcare.com>\\nTo: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>\\nDate: Wed, 09 Jul 2025 15:42:00 -07:00\\nSubject: Re: Data residency/retention and redaction options for PHI - quick questions\\n\\nThanks all \\u2014 that helps a lot. For our internal review, we'll propose 90 days for derived artifacts, 365 for audit trails (exportable), and client-side redaction for direct identifiers. Please go ahead and schedule a 30 min tech call next week; Rishi, I'll ask our infra lead (copied to follow-up) to join.\\n\\nSarah\\nSarah Mills\\nDirector, Security Compliance, Harbor Healthcare\\n\"\n  ],\n  \"title_field_name\": \"subject\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"messages\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_9d01b1a924fd4ee994233893b1096d8a\"\n}",

      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Sanitization policy options and residency/retention for PHI - Q&A\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/gmail\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/gmail/ben_carter/20250708-sanitization-policy-options-for-regulated-healthcare-qna.json\nConnector: gmail\nWorkspace: ben_carter\n\na short playbook ( redwood - sanitization - options - v1. pdf ) and an example audit export. retention ( recommended default tiers ) - 30 days : lowest cost + simplest ( good for ephemeral chat / triage ). minimal log retention, fast kv - cache eviction. - 90 days : common compromise for non - longitudinal phi artifacts ( summaries, annotations ). allows short - term troubleshooting and a / b quality checks. - 365 days : used when business / legal requires year - long traces ( billing disputes, clinical continuity ). higher storage and audit complexity. tradeoffs : shorter windows reduce storage and retention of cached embeddings ; longer windows increase cost and require stronger key management and rotation policies.",

  ],
  "messages": [
    "From: Sarah Mills <sarah.mills@harborhealthcare.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: legal@harborhealthcare.com
Date: Tue, 08 Jul 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Data residency/retention and redaction options for PHI - quick questions

Hi Ben,

Thanks for the demo last week. We have a follow-up from our security and compliance team: two quick, high-level questions to help us scope an internal decision.

1) Retention limits: for PHI-derived outputs (summaries, annotations) what typical retention windows do you recommend for regulated healthcare customers? We need a short list (e.g., 30/90/365 days) that maps to tradeoffs you see in cost and operational complexity.

2) Redaction/sanitization options: we want to understand realistic approaches you support for removing or obfuscating PHI at ingest and at rest. Specifically: field-level permanent redaction, reversible tokenization, pseudonymization, and whether redaction can be applied retroactively to cached request/response artifacts.

Also: what logs/audit evidence can you provide to satisfy an external audit request (timestamped deletion events, exportable audit logs, and proof of KV-cache flushes)?

Appreciate concise answers we can pass to our legal/compliance folks. If it helps, we can schedule 30 min with Rishi and your security engineer.

Best,
Sarah
Director, Security Compliance
Harbor Healthcare

Attachments: none

    "From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Mills <sarah.mills@harborhealthcare.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 08 Jul 2025 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Data residency/retention and redaction options for PHI - quick questions

Hi Sarah — great questions. Below is a pragmatic breakdown you can share with legal/compliance. I kept it concise and highlighted tradeoffs. Attaching a short playbook (redwood-sanitization-options-v1.pdf) and an example audit export.

Retention (recommended default tiers)
- 30 days: lowest cost + simplest (good for ephemeral chat/triage). Minimal log retention, fast KV-cache eviction.
- 90 days: common compromise for non-longitudinal PHI artifacts (summaries, annotations). Allows short-term troubleshooting and A/B quality checks.
- 365 days: used when business/legal requires year-long traces (billing disputes, clinical continuity). Higher storage and audit complexity.
Tradeoffs: shorter windows reduce storage and retention of cached embeddings; longer windows increase cost and require stronger key management and rotation policies.

Sanitization / Redaction options we support
1) Pre-ingest field-level redaction: non-reversible removal of named fields before any tokenization or embedding. Strongest guarantee if done client-side or at gateway.
2) Server-side deterministic pseudonymization: replace identifiers with consistent pseudonyms (useful when you need linkage but not original value). Reversibility depends on where the mapping store lives — we recommend customer-managed KMS + mapping store for reversible mapping.
3) Tokenization (reversible): we can integrate with customer token vaults (customer-managed) for reversible tokens; requires contractual controls if reversible.
4) Post-ingest scrub + reingest: we support a scrub pipeline that can retroactively remove fields and then re-ingest sanitized artifacts — works for stored artifacts but not for in-memory KV cache unless cache flush is triggered (see below).

Cache/Runtime considerations
- KV cache: we provide an API to invalidate/flush per-tenant caches. Flushing is immediate for active processes but you should plan a short rollback window if you rely on prefix caching for latency.
- Embeddings and derived artifacts: if embeddings were persisted externally (DB or vector store) we provide scripts and tooling to locate and remove vectors by metadata tag. Note that embeddings derived from sensitive text are irreversible; redaction removes the original text but cannot 'ungenerate' vectors already used by downstream stores without explicit deletion.

Auditability / Evidence for audits
- Exportable audit logs: timestamped events (object created, deleted, redaction applied, cache flush) with request IDs. Provided as CSV/JSON exports.
- Deletion proof: we can provide signed deletion events (hash+timestamp) for storage objects.
- Access logs: token-level access trails available via Console with retention window matching your plan.

Next steps: I copied Marissa to coordinate Contract/SOW needs and Rishi (our security lead) to chime in on the KMS/mapping specifics. Would you like 30 minutes tomorrow or Friday for a quick walkthrough?

Regards,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0189

Attachments: redwood-sanitization-options-v1.pdf (PDF), example-audit-log-export.csv (CSV)
",

    "From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Data residency/retention and redaction options for PHI - quick questions

Hi Sarah — Rishi from Security. A few technical clarifications to help your controls team evaluate risk: 

1) Strongest guarantees: pre-ingest client-side redaction or gateway-level transformation (never leave original data on disk) is the most robust for regulated PHI. If you must preserve originals, keep mapping tokens in customer-owned stores (VPC-hosted DB) with strict KMS access.

2) Retroactive removal: we can delete objects and issue signed deletion receipts. For runtime artifacts:
   - KV cache: we support tenant-scoped eviction calls (immediate). We persist cache-invalidation events to audit logs.
   - Worker / GPU memory: clearing memory is immediate but cannot be retroactively validated after process termination; rely on deletion receipts for persisted artifacts.

3) Embeddings: treat them as primary artifacts — if you need them removed, we will run metadata-tag based deletion across vector stores and provide a deletion report. Note: if third-party vector stores exist outside the Redwood environment, deletion will require coordination.

4) Proof for auditors: we provide
   - Signed deletion receipts (SHA256 digest + timestamp + signer id)
   - Exportable audit logs with event types and correlation IDs
   - Evidence of KMS rotations and CMK metadata (when customer-managed KMS is used)

5) Operational playbook we recommend for regulated workflows:
   - Define retention tier per artifact class (raw transcript, summary, annotations, embeddings)
   - Enforce client-side redaction for raw identifiers where possible
   - Use pseudonymization for analytics cohorts where linkage is needed
   - Schedule regular deletion jobs and capture signed receipts
   - Monitor cache eviction and record events in the audit stream

I can walk your engineers through the KMS integration and the deletion API. If Harbor needs us to run a one-off scrub to bring an existing dataset into compliance, we will propose a timeboxed engagement with a deletion report.

This ticket captures support engagement, investigation notes, and mitigation steps.\",\n  \"steps_to_reproduce\": [\n    \"1) From an eu-west client, send a streaming chat request to /v1/chat/stream with rw-chat-3.0 and typical prompt (~800 tokens).\",\n    \"2) Observe SDK stream open then long silence; client eventually receives timeout at 120s or sees partial tokens then disconnect.\",\n    \"3) Check request routing headers X-Region-Routed-To and X-Routing-Policy in logs; observed value: us-east for affected requests.\",\n    \"4) Correlate with smart-router decisions in routing logs and with api-gateway connection traces to confirm cross-region proxied connections.\"\n  ],\n  \"logs\": [\n    \"2026-03-12T10:42:11Z gateway[req-9a3d]: routed request region=eu-west -> target=us-east (route_policy=latency_fallback) ttl=30s\",\n    \"2026-03-12T10:42:13Z smart-router[decision]: evaluated peers: eu-edge-12 healthy=false last_check=00:20:07; selected us-edge-3 score=0.72\",\n    \"2026-03-12T10:44:55Z runtime[serve-42]: token-gen start id=req-9a3d latency_probe=0.0\",\n    \"2026-03-12T10:46:37Z runtime[serve-42]: token-gen long-tail: rpc to us-east backend RTT=128ms queue-wait=88s -> 504 threshold exceeded\",\n    \"2026-03-12T11:02:10Z sdk-client[inkwell]: stream disconnected with error: read timeout after 120s\"\n  ],\n  \"investigation_notes\": [\n    \"Initial hypothesis: smart-router fallback to us-east due to transient eu-west peering health check failures (cloud provider reported BGP flaps).\",\n    \"Checked smart-router health checks: multiple eu-west edge peers marked unhealthy simultaneously; health-check interval set to 15s, but TTL for peer negative caching was 30s leading to over-eager failover.\",\n    \"Observed mismatch: routing rollout (PR #187) changed the fallback scoring weights last week and reduced locality bias; combination of health-check flaps and lower locality weight caused bulk reroute.\",\n    \"Metric correlation: spike in cross-region egress and RPC SLO violations coincident with peering event logged by provider (see provider status page).\",\n    \"Reproducibility: can reproduce by forcing eu-edge peers to 'unhealthy' in staging smart-router and observing routing to us-east and increased RTTs; confirms routing decision path.\"\n  ],\n  \"customer_comments\": [\n    \"2026-03-12 10:50 UTC - Inkwell support: \\\"We're seeing many streaming sessions drop and SDK timeouts, impacting customer demos. Can you confirm region is eu?\\\"\",\n    \"2026-03-12 11:10 UTC - Inkwell support: \\\"Partial recovery observed after 11:05 but still seeing increased latency for some requests. Please advise on mitigation and ETA for root cause fix.\\\"\"\n  ],\n  \"mitigation\": \"At 11:05 UTC ops pinned routing policy for enterprise customers in eu-west to prefer in-region endpoints and increased health-check sensitivity to avoid blackholing on brief flaps. Added temporary rate-limit exemptions for affected customer to reduce retry storms.\",\n  \"resolution\": \"Temporary: pinned eu-west routes for enterprise customers and rolled back upstream routing weight change (PR #187) that reduced locality bias. Permanent: schedule change to health-check negative caching TTL and add continuous test that simulates peering flaps to validate routing behavior. Follow-up task created to harden smart-router scoring algorithm (INT-412).\",\n  \"resolution_notes\": \"Customers recovered to baseline by 11:25 UTC after pinning. Post-incident, we will deploy: 1) revert routing weight change in production (done 2026-03-12 11:45 UTC), 2) lower negative-cache TTL to 5s for edge peer health, 3) add canary that simulates transient peer failure. Owner: Maya Patel / Networking team.\",\n  \"next_steps\": [\n    \"Schedule code rollback verification for routing PR #187 in staging (owner: infra-team).\",\n    \"Create automated integration test for peering flaps in CI (owner: SRE).\",\n    \"Contact cloud provider to request postmortem for the eu-west peering anomaly and retain their timeline (owner: Partnerships).\",\n    \"Communicate summary and RCA draft to Inkwell and impacted customers (owner: CS - Nora Vega).\"\n  ],\n  \"title_field_name\": \"summary\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"description\",\n    \"steps_to_reproduce\",\n    \"logs\",\n    \"investigation_notes\",\n    \"customer_comments\",\n    \"mitigation\",\n    \"resolution\",\n    \"resolution_notes\",\n    \"next_steps\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_a6242651cc144f53bc7fe653dddfc8de\"\n}",
