      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Intermittent request timeouts for EU customers caused by cross-region routing to us-east during peering flap\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/jira\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/jira/customer-support/SUP-7813-eu-routing-peering-latency-fanout.json\nConnector: jira\nWorkspace: customer-support\nProject: customer-support\n\n- initial hypothesis : smart - router fallback to us - east due to transient eu - west peering health check failures ( cloud provider reported bgp flaps ). - checked smart - router health checks : multiple eu - west edge peers marked unhealthy simultaneously ; health - check interval set to 15s, but ttl for peer negative caching was 30s leading to over - eager failover. - observed mismatch : routing rollout ( pr # 187 ) changed the fallback scoring weights last week and reduced locality bias ; combination of health - check flaps and lower locality weight caused bulk reroute. - metric correlation : spike in cross - region egress and rpc slo violations coincident with peering event logged by provider ( see provider status",

document.title: Intermittent request timeouts for EU customers caused by cross-region routing to us-east during peering flap
document.content:
{
  "key": "SUP-7813",
  "project": "customer-support",
  "issue_type": "Incident",
  "summary": "Intermittent request timeouts for EU customers caused by cross-region routing to us-east during peering flap",
  "status": "In Progress",
  "priority": "P1",
  "severity": "Sev1",
  "created_at": "2026-03-12",
  "updated_at": "2026-03-13",
  "reporter": "Jared Coleman",
  "assignee": "Maya Patel",
  "customer_company": "Inkwell Analytics",
  "customer_tier": "enterprise",
  "components": [
    "api-gateway",
    "smart-router",
    "serving-runtime",
    "network"
  ],
  "labels": [
    "latency",
    "cross-region-routing",
    "peering",
    "timeouts",
    "streaming"
  ],
  "environment": "prod (eu-west)",
  "affected_models": [
    "rw-instruct-2.7",
    "rw-chat-3.0"
  ],
  "affected_regions": [
    "eu-west",
    "us-east"
  ],
  "sla_due_at": "2026-03-12T15:00:00Z",
  "first_response_due_at": "2026-03-12T12:00:00Z",
  "linked_issues": [
    "SUP-7710",
    "INT-402"
  ],
  "related_incident_id": "INC-2026-0312-05",
  "related_github_prs": [
    "https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing/pull/187",
    "https://github.com/redwood-inference/inference-runtime/pull/939"
  ],
  "related_confluence_pages": [
    "https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OPS/pages/Regional+Routing+Runbook"
  ],
  "description": "Issue summary: Since 2026-03-12 10:40 UTC we have received multiple reports from EU customers (notably Inkwell Analytics) of high tail latency and request timeouts for text-generation and streaming responses. Impact: A subset of requests from eu-west were being routed to us-east (round-trip +120ms) causing queueing in serving runtime and SDK-level timeouts for streaming sessions. Environment: prod (eu-west); affected customers primarily enterprise tier. Timeline: 10:35 - spike begins; 10:40 - first customer report; 10:52 - alerting hit p1 threshold; 11:05 - mitigation pinned region routing; 11:20 - partial recovery for pinned routes; 12:00 - continued investigation. Observed behavior: large fraction of streaming sessions fail with: SDK error: \"read timeout after 120s\" and gateway 504s when backend token generation exceeded 110s. Cross-region latency correlated with a peering degradation reported by cloud provider in eu-west peering fabric. This ticket captures support engagement, investigation notes, and mitigation steps.",
  "steps_to_reproduce": [
    "1) From an eu-west client, send a streaming chat request to /v1/chat/stream with rw-chat-3.0 and typical prompt (~800 tokens).",
    "2) Observe SDK stream open then long silence; client eventually receives timeout at 120s or sees partial tokens then disconnect.",
    "3) Check request routing headers X-Region-Routed-To and X-Routing-Policy in logs; observed value: us-east for affected requests.",
    "4) Correlate with smart-router decisions in routing logs and with api-gateway connection traces to confirm cross-region proxied connections."
  ],
  "logs": [
    "2026-03-12T10:42:11Z gateway[req-9a3d]: routed request region=eu-west -> target=us-east (route_policy=latency_fallback) ttl=30s",
    "2026-03-12T10:42:13Z smart-router[decision]: evaluated peers: eu-edge-12 healthy=false last_check=00:20:07; selected us-edge-3 score=0.72",
    "2026-03-12T10:44:55Z runtime[serve-42]: token-gen start id=req-9a3d latency_probe=0.0",
    "2026-03-12T10:46:37Z runtime[serve-42]: token-gen long-tail: rpc to us-east backend RTT=128ms queue-wait=88s -> 504 threshold exceeded",
    "2026-03-12T11:02:10Z sdk-client[inkwell]: stream disconnected with error: read timeout after 120s"
  ],
  "investigation_notes": [
    "Initial hypothesis: smart-router fallback to us-east due to transient eu-west peering health check failures (cloud provider reported BGP flaps).",
    "Checked smart-router health checks: multiple eu-west edge peers marked unhealthy simultaneously; health-check interval set to 15s, but TTL for peer negative caching was 30s leading to over-eager failover.",
    "Observed mismatch: routing rollout (PR #187) changed the fallback scoring weights last week and reduced locality bias; combination of health-check flaps and lower locality weight caused bulk reroute.",
    "Metric correlation: spike in cross-region egress and RPC SLO violations coincident with peering event logged by provider (see provider status page).",
    "Reproducibility: can reproduce by forcing eu-edge peers to 'unhealthy' in staging smart-router and observing routing to us-east and increased RTTs; confirms routing decision path."
  ],
  "customer_comments": [
    "2026-03-12 10:50 UTC - Inkwell support: \"We're seeing many streaming sessions drop and SDK timeouts, impacting customer demos. Can you confirm region is eu?\"",
    "2026-03-12 11:10 UTC - Inkwell support: \"Partial recovery observed after 11:05 but still seeing increased latency for some requests. Please advise on mitigation and ETA for root cause fix.\""
  ],
  "mitigation": "At 11:05 UTC ops pinned routing policy for enterprise customers in eu-west to prefer in-region endpoints and increased health-check sensitivity to avoid blackholing on brief flaps. Added temporary rate-limit exemptions for affected customer to reduce retry storms.",
  "resolution": "Temporary: pinned eu-west routes for enterprise customers and rolled back upstream routing weight change (PR #187) that reduced locality bias. Permanent: schedule change to health-check negative caching TTL and add continuous test that simulates peering flaps to validate routing behavior. Follow-up task created to harden smart-router scoring algorithm (INT-412).",
  "resolution_notes": "Customers recovered to baseline by 11:25 UTC after pinning. Post-incident, we will deploy: 1) revert routing weight change in production (done 2026-03-12 11:45 UTC), 2) lower negative-cache TTL to 5s for edge peer health, 3) add canary that simulates transient peer failure. Owner: Maya Patel / Networking team.",
  "next_steps": [
    "Schedule code rollback verification for routing PR #187 in staging (owner: infra-team).",
    "Create automated integration test for peering flaps in CI (owner: SRE).",
    "Contact cloud provider to request postmortem for the eu-west peering anomaly and retain their timeline (owner: Partnerships).",
    "Communicate summary and RCA draft to Inkwell and impacted customers (owner: CS - Nora Vega)."
  ],
  "title_field_name": "summary",

    "resolution",
    "resolution_notes",
    "next_steps"
  ],

}

# Hosted API retention rule

Status: Support-facing canonical rule (corrected v3)  
Owner: Platform & Console — Ethan Park  
Last validated: 2026-08-01  
Replaces: interim v1 at this same path

## Customer-facing rule

Unless an executed enterprise contract, DPA, or residency addendum says otherwise:

- **Request/response payload logs:** retained 30 days by default. Enterprise contracts may configure 90 or 365 days.
- **Streaming and KV caches:** ephemeral; held in memory or short local caches for less than one hour unless the customer explicitly elects persistence.
- **Embeddings and derived vectors:** retained 14 days by default; a 7-day strict-ephemeral option is available. Longer storage applies only when the customer elects persistent vector storage under an SLA.
- **Model artifacts:** model snapshots and fine-tuned artifacts remain until explicitly deleted. Rolling backup snapshots have a 30-day default.
- **Verified erasure or tenant termination:** serving stops immediately and the tenant dataset is marked for purge. Primary data is purged within 30 days. Backups and replicated snapshots are scrubbed within 90 days. A deletion attestation/certificate is available after completion on request.
- **Backups:** backup retention is at most 90 days by default; longer retention requires agreement. Backups may replicate to a secondary region for disaster recovery according to the customer SLA.
- **EU-only custody:** available only with the hosted-enterprise data-residency addendum. For an EU-only contract, backups remain in-region and cross-region replication is disabled unless explicitly contracted.
- **Encryption and audit evidence:** cloud KMS protects data at rest by default. Enterprise customers may use customer-managed keys; HSM integration applies to Private deployments. Deletion and erasure events are retained in the audit trail for 365 days and may be surfaced in Console or exported for enterprise customers. Events include the actor, timestamp, object ID, and operation status.

Use “within 30 days” only for primary purge after a **verified** erasure request or tenant termination. Do not describe that as immediate physical deletion. Immediate action is cessation of serving and purge marking.

## Residency and cross-region caution

Hosted data is persisted in the tenancy's assigned primary region. Self-serve tenancy is assigned to a nearby regional cluster and is US by default for the cited questionnaire; support must check the actual tenant mapping rather than promise a country or cloud region from sign-up location alone.

Runtime fallback can route requests across regions when locality fails: incident SUP-7813 records EU-west traffic routed to US-east under the latency-fallback policy. Therefore region preference, primary storage region, runtime routing, DR replication, and backup custody are distinct. Only a controlling contract/addendum and deployed routing/backup configuration establish a residency promise.

## Remaining unknowns and limits

The evidence does not establish:

- deletion timing for customer-controlled or third-party vector stores;
- a generally available guarantee that worker/GPU-memory clearing can be retroactively proven after process termination;
- that every enterprise account has CMK/HSM, Console export, or a signed receipt without configuration or request;
- retention for aggregated or de-identified telemetry;
- a universal no-cross-region runtime-routing promise outside a controlling residency contract and verified configuration;
- whether a particular contract extends defaults.

## Validation before answering a questionnaire

1. Verify deployment mode and the executed order form, DPA, SLA, and residency addendum.
2. Name the data class precisely; never use “logs” without distinguishing payload logs, audit events, access logs, and aggregated telemetry.
3. Confirm the tenant's primary-region mapping, runtime fallback policy, DR target, and backup replication policy.
4. Confirm configured TTLs and recent expiration-job evidence.
5. Require a verified erasure/termination request before quoting the purge clock.
6. Coordinate deletion of third-party stores and request the deletion attestation only after the applicable purge completes.
7. For audit evidence, collect configuration, expiration alerts, event exports, deletion receipts where applicable, and KMS/CMK metadata.

## Authoritative evidence

- [Hosted API: Data geography, TTL & purge cadence — security questionnaire response](/knowledge/company/sources/gmail/aditya_rao/20260602-crestline-residency-ttl-playbook-response.json) (`dsid_7c0ce3505c1d46d8a00aa6680c35fbd3`): infrastructure-product-confirmed answers sent externally, covering data classes, erasure/termination, backups, EU-only custody, KMS, and audit retention.
- [Sanitization policy options and residency/retention for PHI — Q&A](/knowledge/company/sources/gmail/ben_carter/20250708-sanitization-policy-options-for-regulated-healthcare-qna.json) (`dsid_9d01b1a924fd4ee994233893b1096d8a`): Head of Security clarification on signed deletion receipts, cache eviction, embeddings, third-party stores, and evidence limits.
- [SUP-7813: EU requests routed to US-east during peering flap](/knowledge/company/sources/jira/customer-support/SUP-7813-eu-routing-peering-latency-fanout.json) (`dsid_a6242651cc144f53bc7fe653dddfc8de`): production evidence that runtime fallback can cross regions.

# Hosted API retention rule

Status: Support-facing canonical rule (corrected v3)  
Owner: Platform & Console — Ethan Park  
Last validated: 2026-08-01  
Replaces: interim v1 at this same path

## Customer-facing rule

Unless an executed enterprise contract, DPA, or residency addendum says otherwise:

- **Request/response payload logs:** retained 30 days by default. Enterprise contracts may configure 90 or 365 days.
- **Streaming and KV caches:** ephemeral; held in memory or short local caches for less than one hour unless the customer explicitly elects persistence.
- **Embeddings and derived vectors:** retained 14 days by default; a 7-day strict-ephemeral option is available. Longer storage applies only when the customer elects persistent vector storage under an SLA.
- **Model artifacts:** model snapshots and fine-tuned artifacts remain until explicitly deleted. Rolling backup snapshots have a 30-day default.
- **Verified erasure or tenant termination:** serving stops immediately and the tenant dataset is marked for purge. Primary data is purged within 30 days. Backups and replicated snapshots are scrubbed within 90 days. A deletion attestation/certificate is available after completion on request.
- **Backups:** backup retention is at most 90 days by default; longer retention requires agreement. Backups may replicate to a secondary region for disaster recovery according to the customer SLA.
- **EU-only custody:** available only with the hosted-enterprise data-residency addendum. For an EU-only contract, backups remain in-region and cross-region replication is disabled unless explicitly contracted.
- **Encryption and audit evidence:** cloud KMS protects data at rest by default. Enterprise customers may use customer-managed keys; HSM integration applies to Private deployments. Deletion and erasure events are retained in the audit trail for 365 days and may be surfaced in Console or exported for enterprise customers. Events include the actor, timestamp, object ID, and operation status.

Use “within 30 days” only for primary purge after a **verified** erasure request or tenant termination. Do not describe that as immediate physical deletion. Immediate action is cessation of serving and purge marking.

              "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Hosted API retention support rule corrected v3\nSource: agent-memory\nPath: /memory/semantic_memory/hosted-api-retention-support-rule-corrected-v3-ected_v3.md\nWorkspace: agent-memory\nTeam: Ethan Park\n\n# Hosted API retention support rule corrected v3\n\nMemory type: semantic_memory\nRecorded: 2026-08-01T00:00:00Z\nConfidence: 0.95\nOwner: Ethan Park\nTags: hosted-api, retention, deletion, residency, support, corrected-v3\n\n## Summary\n\nCanonical Hosted API support rule: request/response payload logs default to 30 days (90/365 only by enterprise contract); embeddings default to 14 days with a 7-day option; caches are ephemeral under one hour unless persisted; model artifacts remain until deleted and rolling snapshots default to 30 days. After verified erasure or tenant termination, serving stops immediately, primary data is purged within 30 days, and backups/replicated snapshots within 90 days, with attestation available after completion.               "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Hosted API retention rule\nSource: Redwood Platform & Console\nPath: /knowledge/policies/hosted-api-retention.md\nWorkspace: task/ethan-park/retention-rule-v1-v3\n\n# Hosted API retention rule\n\nStatus: Support-facing interim rule (v1)  \nOwner: Platform & Console — Ethan Park  \nLast validated: 2026-08-01\n\n## Supported guidance\n\n- Hosted API-level logs are retained for 90 days by default.\n- Longer log retention may be available as an add-on. Private deployments can instead forward logs to a customer SIEM; support must confirm the applicable order form and deployment configuration before promising either option.\n- Treat configured region and runtime fallback as separate controls. Product acceptance criteria require fallback routing to produce an explicit audit event. This evidence does **not** establish that standard Hosted API data is region-locked or that fallback never crosses regions.\n- For audit validation, collect the retention configuration, a representative log export, the retention-policy document, and retention-expiration alerts. The assurance memo is a draft evidence checklist, not a customer commitment.\n\n## Unknowns — do not promise\n\nCurrent evidence does not establish:\n\n- retention periods for request or response payloads, embeddings, model artifacts, or aggregated metrics;\n- deletion timing for active indexes, primary stores, caches, analytics copies, snapshots, or backups;\n- timing after tenant termination or an erasure request;\n- whether backups replicate across regions, their maximum retention, or whether an EU-only/US-only custody option covers backups;\n- availability, format, or retention of deletion receipts, certificates, or customer-visible audit events;\n- a default Hosted API storage country or a contractual residency guarantee.\n\nSupport must not translate the 90-day API-log statement into a purge SLA or a payload-retention promise.\n\n## Validation before answering a questionnaire",

              "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Hosted API retention rule\nSource: Redwood Platform & Console\nPath: /knowledge/policies/hosted-api-retention.md\nWorkspace: task/ethan-park/retention-rule-correction-v3\n\n# Hosted API retention rule\n\nStatus: Support-facing canonical rule (corrected v3)  \nOwner: Platform & Console — Ethan Park  \nLast validated: 2026-08-01  \nReplaces: interim v1 at this same path\n\n## Customer-facing rule\n\nUnless an executed enterprise contract, DPA, or residency addendum says otherwise:\n\n- **Request/response payload logs:** retained 30 days by default. Enterprise contracts may configure 90 or 365 days.\n- **Streaming and KV caches:** ephemeral; held in memory or short local caches for less than one hour unless the customer explicitly elects persistence.\n- **Embeddings and derived vectors:** retained 14 days by default; a 7-day strict-ephemeral option is available. Longer storage applies only when the customer elects persistent vector storage under an SLA.\n- **Model artifacts:** model snapshots and fine-tuned artifacts remain until explicitly deleted. Rolling backup snapshots have a 30-day default.\n- **Verified erasure or tenant termination:** serving stops immediately and the tenant dataset is marked for purge. Primary data is purged within 30 days. Backups and replicated snapshots are scrubbed within 90 days. A deletion attestation/certificate is available after completion on request.\n- **Backups:** backup retention is at most 90 days by default; longer retention requires agreement. Backups may replicate to a secondary region for disaster recovery according to the customer SLA.\n- **EU-only custody:** available only with the hosted-enterprise data-residency addendum. For an EU-only contract, backups remain in-region and cross-region replication is disabled unless explicitly contracted.\n- **Encryption and audit evidence:** cloud KMS protects data at rest by default. Enterprise customers may use customer-managed keys; HSM integration applies to Private deployments. Deletion and erasure events are retained in the audit trail for 365 days and may be surfaced in Console or exported for enterprise customers. Events include the actor, timestamp, object ID, and operation status.\n\nUse “within 30 days” only for primary purge after a **verified** erasure request or tenant termination. Do not describe that as immediate physical deletion. Immediate action is cessation of serving and purge marking.\n\n## Residency and cross-region caution",

              "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Hosted API retention rule\nSource: Redwood Platform & Console\nPath: /knowledge/policies/hosted-api-retention.md\nWorkspace: task/ethan-park/retention-rule-v1-v3\n\n- availability, format, or retention of deletion receipts, certificates, or customer-visible audit events;\n- a default Hosted API storage country or a contractual residency guarantee.\n\nSupport must not translate the 90-day API-log statement into a purge SLA or a payload-retention promise.\n\n## Validation before answering a questionnaire\n\n1. Identify Hosted, Dedicated, or Private deployment and obtain the executed order form/DPA and any residency amendment.\n2. Confirm the exact data class: API metadata, prompt/response payload, embedding, artifact, audit event, cache, analytic copy, or backup.\n3. Ask Platform/SRE for the deployed retention configuration and expiration-job evidence.\n4. Ask Security/Privacy for approved deletion, backup, residency, and attestation language.\n5. For residency, verify both the primary region and every fallback/DR and backup path.\n6. Escalate any requested deletion or residency SLA until a controlling policy or contract is cited.\n\n## Evidence\n\n- [Larkview HealthTech onboarding & risk handoff](/knowledge/company/sources/fireflies/customer-success/2026-04-02-larkview-healthtech-onboarding-risk-handoff.json) (`dsid_1ceb67c562a647838ca1b925f4187553`): Redwood states a 90-day default for hosted API-level logs; extended retention is an add-on, and Private can push logs to the customer SIEM. Transcript quality is marked medium.\n- [Residency fallback pricing and launch acceptance criteria](/knowledge/company/sources/slack/product/1767123456-residency-fallback-pricing-and-launch-ask-negotiation.json) (`dsid_d9a15ab8f79c4c7e938f90cf3586da13`): fallback must be tested and explicitly audit-logged; it does not itself establish a residency promise.\n- [Assurance micro memo: quick SOC 2 control probes](/knowledge/company/sources/google_drive/users/assurance-micro-memo-haruki-2026.json) (`dsid_c0a03597cb93476b9904666e1aedd6e0`): draft checklist for retention-control evidence and unresolved assurance questions.",

              "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Hosted API retention rule\nSource: Redwood Platform & Console\nPath: /knowledge/policies/hosted-api-retention.md\nWorkspace: task/ethan-park/retention-rule-correction-v3\n\ninclude the actor, timestamp, object ID, and operation status.\n\nUse “within 30 days” only for primary purge after a **verified** erasure request or tenant termination. Do not describe that as immediate physical deletion. Immediate action is cessation of serving and purge marking.\n\n## Residency and cross-region caution\n\nHosted data is persisted in the tenancy's assigned primary region. Self-serve tenancy is assigned to a nearby regional cluster and is US by default for the cited questionnaire; support must check the actual tenant mapping rather than promise a country or cloud region from sign-up location alone.\n\nRuntime fallback can route requests across regions when locality fails: incident SUP-7813 records EU-west traffic routed to US-east under the latency-fallback policy. Therefore region preference, primary storage region, runtime routing, DR replication, and backup custody are distinct. Only a controlling contract/addendum and deployed routing/backup configuration establish a residency promise.\n\n## Remaining unknowns and limits\n\nThe evidence does not establish:\n\n- deletion timing for customer-controlled or third-party vector stores;\n- a generally available guarantee that worker/GPU-memory clearing can be retroactively proven after process termination;\n- that every enterprise account has CMK/HSM, Console export, or a signed receipt without configuration or request;\n- retention for aggregated or de-identified telemetry;\n- a universal no-cross-region runtime-routing promise outside a controlling residency contract and verified configuration;\n- whether a particular contract extends defaults.\n\n## Validation before answering a questionnaire\n\n1. Verify deployment mode and the executed order form, DPA, SLA, and residency addendum.\n2. Name the data class precisely; never use “logs” without distinguishing payload logs, audit events, access logs, and aggregated telemetry.\n3. Confirm the tenant's primary-region mapping, runtime fallback policy, DR target, and backup replication policy.\n4. Confirm configured TTLs and recent expiration-job evidence.\n5. Require a verified erasure/termination request before quoting the purge clock.\n6. Coordinate deletion of third-party stores and request the deletion attestation only after the applicable purge completes.\n7. For audit evidence, collect configuration, expiration alerts, event exports, deletion receipts where applicable, and KMS/CMK metadata.\n\n## Authoritative evidence",

            "content": "# Hosted API retention rule\n\nStatus: Support-facing interim rule (v1)  \nOwner: Platform & Console — Ethan Park  \nLast validated: 2026-08-01\n\n## Supported guidance\n\n- Hosted API-level logs are retained for 90 days by default.\n- Longer log retention may be available as an add-on. Private deployments can instead forward logs to a customer SIEM; support must confirm the applicable order form and deployment configuration before promising either option.\n- Treat configured region and runtime fallback as separate controls. Product acceptance criteria require fallback routing to produce an explicit audit event. This evidence does **not** establish that standard Hosted API data is region-locked or that fallback never crosses regions.\n- For audit validation, collect the retention configuration, a representative log export, the retention-policy document, and retention-expiration alerts. The assurance memo is a draft evidence checklist, not a customer commitment.\n\n## Unknowns — do not promise\n\nCurrent evidence does not establish:\n\n- retention periods for request or response payloads, embeddings, model artifacts, or aggregated metrics;\n- deletion timing for active indexes, primary stores, caches, analytics copies, snapshots, or backups;\n- timing after tenant termination or an erasure request;\n- whether backups replicate across regions, their maximum retention, or whether an EU-only/US-only custody option covers backups;\n- availability, format, or retention of deletion receipts, certificates, or customer-visible audit events;\n- a default Hosted API storage country or a contractual residency guarantee.\n\nSupport must not translate the 90-day API-log statement into a purge SLA or a payload-retention promise.\n\n## Validation before answering a questionnaire\n\n1. Identify Hosted, Dedicated, or Private deployment and obtain the executed order form/DPA and any residency amendment.\n2. Confirm the exact data class: API metadata, prompt/response payload, embedding, artifact, audit event, cache, analytic copy, or backup.\n3. Ask Platform/SRE for the deployed retention configuration and expiration-job evidence.\n4. Ask Security/Privacy for approved deletion, backup, residency, and attestation language.\n5. For residency, verify both the primary region and every fallback/DR and backup path.\n6. Escalate any requested deletion or residency SLA until a controlling policy or contract is cited.\n\n## Evidence\n\n- [Larkview HealthTech onboarding & risk handoff](/knowledge/company/sources/fireflies/customer-success/2026-04-02-larkview-healthtech-onboarding-risk-handoff.json) (`dsid_1ceb67c562a647838ca1b925f4187553`): Redwood states a 90-day default for hosted API-level logs; extended retention is an add-on, and Private can push logs to the customer SIEM. Transcript quality is marked medium.\n- [Residency fallback pricing and launch acceptance criteria](/knowledge/company/sources/slack/product/1767123456-residency-fallback-pricing-and-launch-ask-negotiation.json) (`dsid_d9a15ab8f79c4c7e938f90cf3586da13`): fallback must be tested and explicitly audit-logged; it does not itself establish a residency promise.\n- [Assurance micro memo: quick SOC 2 control probes](/knowledge/company/sources/google_drive/users/assurance-micro-memo-haruki-2026.json) (`dsid_c0a03597cb93476b9904666e1aedd6e0`): draft checklist for retention-control evidence and unresolved assurance questions.\n"

Enterprise contracts may configure 90 or 365 days.\n- **Streaming and KV caches:** ephemeral; held in memory or short local caches for less than one hour unless the customer explicitly elects persistence.\n- **Embeddings and derived vectors:** retained 14 days by default; a 7-day strict-ephemeral option is available. Longer storage applies only when the customer elects persistent vector storage under an SLA.\n- **Model artifacts:** model snapshots and fine-tuned artifacts remain until explicitly deleted. Rolling backup snapshots have a 30-day default.\n- **Verified erasure or tenant termination:** serving stops immediately and the tenant dataset is marked for purge. Primary data is purged within 30 days. Backups and replicated snapshots are scrubbed within 90 days. A deletion attestation/certificate is available after completion on request.\n- **Backups:** backup retention is at most 90 days by default; longer retention requires agreement. Backups may replicate to a secondary region for disaster recovery according to the customer SLA.\n- **EU-only custody:** available only with the hosted-enterprise data-residency addendum. For an EU-only contract, backups remain in-region and cross-region replication is disabled unless explicitly contracted.\n- **Encryption and audit evidence:** cloud KMS protects data at rest by default. Enterprise customers may use customer-managed keys; HSM integration applies to Private deployments. Deletion and erasure events are retained in the audit trail for 365 days and may be surfaced in Console or exported for enterprise customers. Events include the actor, timestamp, object ID, and operation status.\n\nUse “within 30 days” only for primary purge after a **verified** erasure request or tenant termination. Do not describe that as immediate physical deletion. Immediate action is cessation of serving and purge marking.\n\n## Residency and cross-region caution\n\nHosted data is persisted in the tenancy's assigned primary region. Self-serve tenancy is assigned to a nearby regional cluster and is US by default for the cited questionnaire; support must check the actual tenant mapping rather than promise a country or cloud region from sign-up location alone.\n\nRuntime fallback can route requests across regions when locality fails: incident SUP-7813 records EU-west traffic routed to US-east under the latency-fallback policy. Therefore region preference, primary storage region, runtime routing, DR replication, and backup custody are distinct. Only a controlling contract/addendum and deployed routing/backup configuration establish a residency promise.\n\n## Remaining unknowns and limits\n\nThe evidence does not establish:\n\n- deletion timing for customer-controlled or third-party vector stores;\n- a generally available guarantee that worker/GPU-memory clearing can be retroactively proven after process termination;\n- that every enterprise account has CMK/HSM, Console export, or a signed receipt without configuration or request;\n- retention for aggregated or de-identified telemetry;\n- a universal no-cross-region runtime-routing promise outside a controlling residency contract and verified configuration;\n- whether a particular contract extends defaults.\n\n## Validation before answering a questionnaire\n\n1. Verify deployment mode and the executed order form, DPA, SLA, and residency addendum.\n2. Name the data class precisely; never use “logs” without distinguishing payload logs, audit events, access logs, and aggregated telemetry.\n3. Confirm the tenant's primary-region mapping, runtime fallback policy, DR target, and backup replication policy.\n4. Confirm configured TTLs and recent expiration-job evidence.\n5. Require a verified erasure/termination request bef",

# Hosted API retention rule

Status: Support-facing interim rule (v1)  
Owner: Platform & Console — Ethan Park  
Last validated: 2026-08-01

## Supported guidance

- Hosted API-level logs are retained for 90 days by default.
- Longer log retention may be available as an add-on. Private deployments can instead forward logs to a customer SIEM; support must confirm the applicable order form and deployment configuration before promising either option.
- Treat configured region and runtime fallback as separate controls. Product acceptance criteria require fallback routing to produce an explicit audit event. This evidence does **not** establish that standard Hosted API data is region-locked or that fallback never crosses regions.
- For audit validation, collect the retention configuration, a representative log export, the retention-policy document, and retention-expiration alerts. The assurance memo is a draft evidence checklist, not a customer commitment.

## Unknowns — do not promise

Current evidence does not establish:

- retention periods for request or response payloads, embeddings, model artifacts, or aggregated metrics;
- deletion timing for active indexes, primary stores, caches, analytics copies, snapshots, or backups;
- timing after tenant termination or an erasure request;
- whether backups replicate across regions, their maximum retention, or whether an EU-only/US-only custody option covers backups;
- availability, format, or retention of deletion receipts, certificates, or customer-visible audit events;
- a default Hosted API storage country or a contractual residency guarantee.

Support must not translate the 90-day API-log statement into a purge SLA or a payload-retention promise.

## Validation before answering a questionnaire

# Hosted API retention rule

Status: Support-facing canonical rule (corrected v3)  
Owner: Platform & Console — Ethan Park  
Last validated: 2026-08-01  
Replaces: interim v1 at this same path

## Customer-facing rule

Unless an executed enterprise contract, DPA, or residency addendum says otherwise:

- **Request/response payload logs:** retained 30 days by default. Enterprise contracts may configure 90 or 365 days.
- **Streaming and KV caches:** ephemeral; held in memory or short local caches for less than one hour unless the customer explicitly elects persistence.
- **Embeddings and derived vectors:** retained 14 days by default; a 7-day strict-ephemeral option is available. Longer storage applies only when the customer elects persistent vector storage under an SLA.
- **Model artifacts:** model snapshots and fine-tuned artifacts remain until explicitly deleted. Rolling backup snapshots have a 30-day default.
- **Verified erasure or tenant termination:** serving stops immediately and the tenant dataset is marked for purge. Primary data is purged within 30 days. Backups and replicated snapshots are scrubbed within 90 days. A deletion attestation/certificate is available after completion on request.
- **Backups:** backup retention is at most 90 days by default; longer retention requires agreement. Backups may replicate to a secondary region for disaster recovery according to the customer SLA.
- **EU-only custody:** available only with the hosted-enterprise data-residency addendum. For an EU-only contract, backups remain in-region and cross-region replication is disabled unless explicitly contracted.
- **Encryption and audit evidence:** cloud KMS protects data at rest by default. Enterprise customers may use customer-managed keys; HSM integration applies to Private deployments. Deletion and erasure events are retained in the audit trail for 365 days and may be surfaced in Console or exported for enterprise customers. Events include the actor, timestamp, object ID, and operation status.

Use “within 30 days” only for primary purge after a **verified** erasure request or tenant termination. Do not describe that as immediate physical deletion. Immediate action is cessation of serving and purge marking.

## Residency and cross-region caution

Support must not translate the 90-day API-log statement into a purge SLA or a payload-retention promise.

## Validation before answering a questionnaire

1. Identify Hosted, Dedicated, or Private deployment and obtain the executed order form/DPA and any residency amendment.
2. Confirm the exact data class: API metadata, prompt/response payload, embedding, artifact, audit event, cache, analytic copy, or backup.
3. Ask Platform/SRE for the deployed retention configuration and expiration-job evidence.
4. Ask Security/Privacy for approved deletion, backup, residency, and attestation language.
5. For residency, verify both the primary region and every fallback/DR and backup path.
6. Escalate any requested deletion or residency SLA until a controlling policy or contract is cited.

Transcript quality is marked medium.
- [Residency fallback pricing and launch acceptance criteria](/knowledge/company/sources/slack/product/1767123456-residency-fallback-pricing-and-launch-ask-negotiation.json) (`dsid_d9a15ab8f79c4c7e938f90cf3586da13`): fallback must be tested and explicitly audit-logged; it does not itself establish a residency promise.
- [Assurance micro memo: quick SOC 2 control probes](/knowledge/company/sources/google_drive/users/assurance-micro-memo-haruki-2026.json) (`dsid_c0a03597cb93476b9904666e1aedd6e0`): draft checklist for retention-control evidence and unresolved assurance questions.

Use “within 30 days” only for primary purge after a **verified** erasure request or tenant termination. Do not describe that as immediate physical deletion. Immediate action is cessation of serving and purge marking.

## Residency and cross-region caution

Hosted data is persisted in the tenancy's assigned primary region. Self-serve tenancy is assigned to a nearby regional cluster and is US by default for the cited questionnaire; support must check the actual tenant mapping rather than promise a country or cloud region from sign-up location alone.

Runtime fallback can route requests across regions when locality fails: incident SUP-7813 records EU-west traffic routed to US-east under the latency-fallback policy. Therefore region preference, primary storage region, runtime routing, DR replication, and backup custody are distinct. Only a controlling contract/addendum and deployed routing/backup configuration establish a residency promise.

## Remaining unknowns and limits

The evidence does not establish:

- deletion timing for customer-controlled or third-party vector stores;
- a generally available guarantee that worker/GPU-memory clearing can be retroactively proven after process termination;
- that every enterprise account has CMK/HSM, Console export, or a signed receipt without configuration or request;
- retention for aggregated or de-identified telemetry;
- a universal no-cross-region runtime-routing promise outside a controlling residency contract and verified configuration;
- whether a particular contract extends defaults.

## Validation before answering a questionnaire

6. Coordinate deletion of third-party stores and request the deletion attestation only after the applicable purge completes.
7. For audit evidence, collect configuration, expiration alerts, event exports, deletion receipts where applicable, and KMS/CMK metadata.

# Hosted API retention rule

Status: Support-facing canonical rule (corrected v3)  
Owner: Platform & Console — Ethan Park  
Last validated: 2026-08-01  
Replaces: interim v1 at this same path

## Customer-facing rule

Unless an executed enterprise contract, DPA, or residency addendum says otherwise:

- **Request/response payload logs:** retained 30 days by default. Enterprise contracts may configure 90 or 365 days.
- **Streaming and KV caches:** ephemeral; held in memory or short local caches for less than one hour unless the customer explicitly elects persistence.
- **Embeddings and derived vectors:** retained 14 days by default; a 7-day strict-ephemeral option is available. Longer storage applies only when the customer elects persistent vector storage under an SLA.
- **Model artifacts:** model snapshots and fine-tuned artifacts remain until explicitly deleted. Rolling backup snapshots have a 30-day default.
- **Verified erasure or tenant termination:** serving stops immediately and the tenant dataset is marked for purge. Primary data is purged within 30 days. Backups and replicated snapshots are scrubbed within 90 days. A deletion attestation/certificate is available after completion on request.
- **Backups:** backup retention is at most 90 days by default; longer retention requires agreement. Backups may replicate to a secondary region for disaster recovery according to the customer SLA.
- **EU-only custody:** available only with the hosted-enterprise data-residency addendum. For an EU-only contract, backups remain in-region and cross-region replication is disabled unless explicitly contracted.
- **Encryption and audit evidence:** cloud KMS protects data at rest by default. Enterprise customers may use customer-managed keys; HSM integration applies to Private deployments. Deletion and erasure events are retained in the audit trail for 365 days and may be surfaced in Console or exported for enterprise customers. Events include the actor, timestamp, object ID, and operation status.

Use “within 30 days” only for primary purge after a **verified** erasure request or tenant termination. Do not describe that as immediate physical deletion. Immediate action is cessation of serving and purge marking.

## Residency and cross-region caution

Hosted data is persisted in the tenancy's assigned primary region. Self-serve tenancy is assigned to a nearby regional cluster and is US by default for the cited questionnaire; support must check the actual tenant mapping rather than promise a country or cloud region from sign-up location alone.

Runtime fallback can route requests across regions when locality fails: incident SUP-7813 records EU-west traffic routed to US-east under the latency-fallback policy. Therefore region preference, primary storage region, runtime routing, DR replication, and backup custody are distinct. Only a controlling contract/addendum and deployed routing/backup configuration establish a residency promise.

## Remaining unknowns and limits

The evidence does not establish:

- deletion timing for customer-controlled or third-party vector stores;
- a generally available guarantee that worker/GPU-memory clearing can be retroactively proven after process termination;
- that every enterprise account has CMK/HSM, Console export, or a signed receipt without configuration or request;
- retention for aggregated or de-identified telemetry;
- a universal no-cross-region runtime-routing promise outside a controlling residency contract and verified configuration;
- whether a particular contract extends defaults.

2. Name the data class precisely; never use “logs” without distinguishing payload logs, audit events, access logs, and aggregated telemetry.
3. Confirm the tenant's primary-region mapping, runtime fallback policy, DR target, and backup replication policy.
4. Confirm configured TTLs and recent expiration-job evidence.
5. Require a verified erasure/termination request bef

      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Hosted API retention rule\nSource: Redwood Platform & Console\nPath: /knowledge/policies/hosted-api-retention.md\nWorkspace: task/ethan-park/retention-rule-correction-v3\n\ninclude the actor, timestamp, object ID, and operation status.\n\nUse “within 30 days” only for primary purge after a **verified** erasure request or tenant termination. Do not describe that as immediate physical deletion. Immediate action is cessation of serving and purge marking.\n\n## Residency and cross-region caution\n\nHosted data is persisted in the tenancy's assigned primary region. Self-serve tenancy is assigned to a nearby regional cluster and is US by default for the cited questionnaire; support must check the actual tenant mapping rather than promise a country or cloud region from sign-up location alone.\n\nRuntime fallback can route requests across regions when locality fails: incident SUP-7813 records EU-west traffic routed to US-east under the latency-fallback policy. Therefore region preference, primary storage region, runtime routing, DR replication, and backup custody are distinct. Only a controlling contract/addendum and deployed routing/backup configuration establish a residency promise.\n\n## Remaining unknowns and limits\n\nThe evidence does not establish:\n\n- deletion timing for customer-controlled or third-party vector stores;\n- a generally available guarantee that worker/GPU-memory clearing can be retroactively proven after process termination;\n- that every enterprise account has CMK/HSM, Console export, or a signed receipt without configuration or request;\n- retention for aggregated or de-identified telemetry;\n- a universal no-cross-region runtime-routing promise outside a controlling residency contract and verified configuration;\n- whether a particular contract extends defaults.\n\n## Validation before answering a questionnaire\n\n1. Verify deployment mode and the executed order form, DPA, SLA, and residency addendum.\n2. Name the data class precisely; never use “logs” without distinguishing payload logs, audit events, access logs, and aggregated telemetry.\n3. Confirm the tenant's primary-region mapping, runtime fallback policy, DR target, and backup replication policy.\n4. Confirm configured TTLs and recent expiration-job evidence.\n5. Require a verified erasure/termination request before quoting the purge clock.\n6. Coordinate deletion of third-party stores and request the deletion attestation only after the applicable purge completes.\n7. For audit evidence, collect configuration, expiration alerts, event exports, deletion receipts where applicable, and KMS/CMK metadata.\n\n## Authoritative evidence",

document.content:
# Hosted API retention rule

Status: Support-facing canonical rule (corrected v3)  
Owner: Platform & Console — Ethan Park  
Last validated: 2026-08-01  
Replaces: interim v1 at this same path

## Customer-facing rule

Unless an executed enterprise contract, DPA, or residency addendum says otherwise:

- **Request/response payload logs:** retained 30 days by default. Enterprise contracts may configure 90 or 365 days.
- **Streaming and KV caches:** ephemeral; held in memory or short local caches for less than one hour unless the customer explicitly elects persistence.
- **Embeddings and derived vectors:** retained 14 days by default; a 7-day strict-ephemeral option is available. Longer storage applies only when the customer elects persistent vector storage under an SLA.
- **Model artifacts:** model snapshots and fine-tuned artifacts remain until explicitly deleted. Rolling backup snapshots have a 30-day default.
- **Verified erasure or tenant termination:** serving stops immediately and the tenant dataset is marked for purge. Primary data is purged within 30 days. Backups and replicated snapshots are scrubbed within 90 days. A deletion attestation/certificate is available after completion on request.
- **Backups:** backup retention is at most 90 days by default; longer retention requires agreement. Backups may replicate to a secondary region for disaster recovery according to the customer SLA.
- **EU-only custody:** available only with the hosted-enterprise data-residency addendum. For an EU-only contract, backups remain in-region and cross-region replication is disabled unless explicitly contracted.
- **Encryption and audit evidence:** cloud KMS protects data at rest by default. Enterprise customers may use customer-managed keys; HSM integration applies to Private deployments. Deletion and erasure events are retained in the audit trail for 365 days and may be surfaced in Console or exported for enterprise customers. Events include the actor, timestamp, object ID, and operation status.

Use “within 30 days” only for primary purge after a **verified** erasure request or tenant termination. Do not describe that as immediate physical deletion. Immediate action is cessation of serving and purge marking.

## Residency and cross-region caution

Hosted data is persisted in the tenancy's assigned primary region. Self-serve tenancy is assigned to a nearby regional cluster and is US by default for the cited questionnaire; support must check the actual tenant mapping rather than promise a country or cloud region from sign-up location alone.

Runtime fallback can route requests across regions when locality fails: incident SUP-7813 records EU-west traffic routed to US-east under the latency-fallback policy. Therefore region preference, primary storage region, runtime routing, DR replication, and backup custody are distinct. Only a controlling contract/addendum and deployed routing/backup configuration establish a residency promise.

## Remaining unknowns and limits

The evidence does not establish:

- deletion timing for customer-controlled or third-party vector stores;
- a generally available guarantee that worker/GPU-memory clearing can be retroactively proven after process termination;
- that every enterprise account has CMK/HSM, Console export, or a signed receipt without configuration or request;
- retention for aggregated or de-identified telemetry;
- a universal no-cross-region runtime-routing promise outside a controlling residency contract and verified configuration;
- whether a particular contract extends defaults.

## Validation before answering a questionnaire

1. Verify deployment mode and the executed order form, DPA, SLA, and residency addendum.
2. Name the data class precisely; never use “logs” without distinguishing payload logs, audit events, access logs, and aggregated telemetry.
3. Confirm the tenant's primary-region mapping, runtime fallback policy, DR target, and backup replication policy.
4. Confirm configured TTLs and recent expiration-job evidence.
5. Require a verified erasure/termination request before quoting the purge clock.
6. Coordinate deletion of third-party stores and request the deletion attestation only after the applicable purge completes.
7. For audit evidence, collect configuration, expiration alerts, event exports, deletion receipts where applicable, and KMS/CMK metadata.

## Authoritative evidence

- [Hosted API: Data geography, TTL & purge cadence — security questionnaire response](/knowledge/company/sources/gmail/aditya_rao/20260602-crestline-residency-ttl-playbook-response.json) (`dsid_7c0ce3505c1d46d8a00aa6680c35fbd3`): infrastructure-product-confirmed answers sent externally, covering data classes, erasure/termination, backups, EU-only custody, KMS, and audit retention.
- [Sanitization policy options and residency/retention for PHI — Q&A](/knowledge/company/sources/gmail/ben_carter/20250708-sanitization-policy-options-for-regulated-healthcare-qna.json) (`dsid_9d01b1a924fd4ee994233893b1096d8a`): Head of Security clarification on signed deletion receipts, cache eviction, embeddings, third-party stores, and evidence limits.
- [SUP-7813: EU requests routed to US-east during peering flap](/knowledge/company/sources/jira/customer-support/SUP-7813-eu-routing-peering-latency-fanout.json) (`dsid_a6242651cc144f53bc7fe653dddfc8de`): production evidence that runtime fallback can cross regions.

# Hosted API retention support rule corrected v3

Memory type: semantic_memory
Recorded: 2026-08-01T00:00:00Z
Confidence: 0.95
Owner: Ethan Park
Tags: hosted-api, retention, deletion, residency, support, corrected-v3

## Summary

Canonical Hosted API support rule: request/response payload logs default to 30 days (90/365 only by enterprise contract); embeddings default to 14 days with a 7-day option; caches are ephemeral under one hour unless persisted; model artifacts remain until deleted and rolling snapshots default to 30 days. After verified erasure or tenant termination, serving stops immediately, primary data is purged within 30 days, and backups/replicated snapshots within 90 days, with attestation available after completion. Backups may replicate for DR; EU-only backup custody requires the hosted-enterprise residency addendum. Deletion/erasure audit events retain for 365 days. Region assignment does not itself prevent cross-region runtime fallback.

After verified erasure or tenant termination, serving stops immediately, primary data is purged within 30 days, and backups/replicated snapshots within 90 days, with attestation available after completion. Backups may replicate for DR; EU-only backup custody requires the hosted-enterprise residency addendum. Deletion/erasure audit events retain for 365 days. Region assignment does not itself prevent cross-region runtime fallback.

include the actor, timestamp, object ID, and operation status.

Use “within 30 days” only for primary purge after a **verified** erasure request or tenant termination. Do not describe that as immediate physical deletion. Immediate action is cessation of serving and purge marking.

## Residency and cross-region caution

Hosted data is persisted in the tenancy's assigned primary region. Self-serve tenancy is assigned to a nearby regional cluster and is US by default for the cited questionnaire; support must check the actual tenant mapping rather than promise a country or cloud region from sign-up location alone.

Runtime fallback can route requests across regions when locality fails: incident SUP-7813 records EU-west traffic routed to US-east under the latency-fallback policy. Therefore region preference, primary storage region, runtime routing, DR replication, and backup custody are distinct. Only a controlling contract/addendum and deployed routing/backup configuration establish a residency promise.

## Remaining unknowns and limits

The evidence does not establish:

- deletion timing for customer-controlled or third-party vector stores;
- a generally available guarantee that worker/GPU-memory clearing can be retroactively proven after process termination;
- that every enterprise account has CMK/HSM, Console export, or a signed receipt without configuration or request;
- retention for aggregated or de-identified telemetry;
- a universal no-cross-region runtime-routing promise outside a controlling residency contract and verified configuration;
- whether a particular contract extends defaults.

## Validation before answering a questionnaire

1. Verify deployment mode and the executed order form, DPA, SLA, and residency addendum.
2. Name the data class precisely; never use “logs” without distinguishing payload logs, audit events, access logs, and aggregated telemetry.
3. Confirm the tenant's primary-region mapping, runtime fallback policy, DR target, and backup replication policy.
4. Confirm configured TTLs and recent expiration-job evidence.
5. Require a verified erasure/termination request before quoting the purge clock.
6. Coordinate deletion of third-party stores and request the deletion attestation only after the applicable purge completes.
7. For audit evidence, collect configuration, expiration alerts, event exports, deletion receipts where applicable, and KMS/CMK metadata.

## Authoritative evidence",

Confidence: 0.95
Owner: Ethan Park
Tags: hosted-api, retention, deletion, residency, support, corrected-v3

## Summary

Canonical Hosted API support rule: request/response payload logs default to 30 days (90/365 only by enterprise contract); embeddings default to 14 days with a 7-day option; caches are ephemeral under one hour unless persisted; model artifacts remain until deleted and rolling snapshots default to 30 days. After verified erasure or tenant termination, serving stops immediately, primary data is purged within 30 days, and backups/replicated snapshots within 90 days, with attestation available after completion. Backups may replicate for DR; EU-only backup custody requires the hosted-enterprise residency addendum. Deletion/erasure audit events retain for 365 days. Region assignment does not itself prevent cross-region runtime fallback.

Use “within 30 days” only for primary purge after a **verified** erasure request or tenant termination. Do not describe that as immediate physical deletion. Immediate action is cessation of serving and purge marking.

## Residency and cross-region caution

Hosted data is persisted in the tenancy's assigned primary region. Self-serve tenancy is assigned to a nearby regional cluster and is US by default for the cited questionnaire; support must check the actual tenant mapping rather than promise a country or cloud region from sign-up location alone.

Runtime fallback can route requests across regions when locality fails: incident SUP-7813 records EU-west traffic routed to US-east under the latency-fallback policy. Therefore region preference, primary storage region, runtime routing, DR replication, and backup custody are distinct. Only a controlling contract/addendum and deployed routing/backup configuration establish a residency promise.

## Remaining unknowns and limits

The evidence does not establish:

- deletion timing for customer-controlled or third-party vector stores;
- a generally available guarantee that worker/GPU-memory clearing can be retroactively proven after process termination;
- that every enterprise account has CMK/HSM, Console export, or a signed receipt without configuration or request;
- retention for aggregated or de-identified telemetry;
- a universal no-cross-region runtime-routing promise outside a controlling residency contract and verified configuration;
- whether a particular contract extends defaults.

## Validation before answering a questionnaire

1. Verify deployment mode and the executed order form, DPA, SLA, and residency addendum.
2. Name the data class precisely; never use “logs” without distinguishing payload logs, audit events, access logs, and aggregated telemetry.
3. Confirm the tenant's primary-region mapping, runtime fallback policy, DR target, and backup replication policy.
4. Confirm configured TTLs and recent expiration-job evidence.
5. Require a verified erasure/termination request before quoting the purge clock.
6. Coordinate deletion of third-party stores and request the deletion attestation only after the applicable purge completes.
7. For audit evidence, collect configuration, expiration alerts, event exports, deletion receipts where applicable, and KMS/CMK metadata.

Completed both publications and replaced the interim guidance with the corrected rule.

### Policy revisions

- v1, document `workspace_18c7cb7529877f59cc016aa5`
  - Path: `/knowledge/policies/hosted-api-retention.md`
  - SHA-256: `33824f473e5b79f6cdfbb00b82ef403328ecebfe92abbba84df9bfc79b429248`
  - Published only the supported 90-day Hosted API-level log statement.
  - Explicitly left payload retention, deletion, backups, tenant termination, and residency unresolved.
  - Included validation and escalation steps.

- Corrected v3, same document and path
  - SHA-256: `65eac4c21fe252f522284eceafd67a6c71f01d9fb4af1e4fd928ca78aa80c1f0`
  - Request/response payload logs: 30 days by default; 90/365 only by enterprise contract.
  - Embeddings: 14 days by default, with a 7-day option.
  - Ephemeral caches: under one hour unless explicitly persisted.
  - Verified erasure/termination: serving stops immediately; primary purge within 30 days; backups and replicated snapshots scrubbed within 90 days.
  - EU-only backup custody requires the enterprise residency addendum.
  - Deletion/erasure audit events: 365 days.
  - Region assignment does not by itself prevent cross-region runtime fallback.
